“See what different areas your money has been spent on and if that aligns with what you want to achieve,” recommends Crichton.

“It might provide a little bit of encouragement to learn and find out that you could have probably saved X, Y, and Z in certain areas and could have got some of your money working harder for you.”

Reset your budget

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

“Do a bit of a budget reset and take stock of where everything is going,” recommends Crichton.

“People often think of budgets as restrictive, whereas I would encourage people to think of a budget as knowing where everything is going.”

If you have never made a budget before, there are lots of apps that can help.

“Some bank accounts will show you where all your expenses are going, will help you set a budget and will help categorise all your spending,” says Crichton.

“Alternatively, you could just set up a Excel spreadsheet that contains all your different categories of spending.”

Identify areas where you could cut costs

“Take a bit of time and see if you can get a better deal on things like utilities or or subscriptions and see if you can switch to a cheaper provider,” recommends Crichton.

Consider switching banks

“Keep an eye on the amount of interest that your bank accounts are getting,” recommends Crichton.

Tidy up old pensions

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

The end of summer and the start of a new school year is the perfect time to tackle any pension admin.

“See if you need to tidy up any old pensions that you’ve left at previous employers,” recommends Crichton.

“You might have various small workplace pensions that you might want to look at consolidating. Make sure that your pensions are working hard for you, rather than forgetting about them.”

Review ISAs

September is a great time to review ISAs because it marks the start of the autumn financial planning season, roughly midway through the UK tax year.

“When we’re moving into September, it’s only seven months until the end of the tax year, so if you want to do things like put money in ISAs, it’s a good time to do this,” says Crichton.

“If you put this off until Christmas or January, then you might not have the time to utilise your ISA.”

Think about longer-term goals

“Think about what longer-term objectives you want to be achieving – whether that’s retirement or saving for a property purchase,” advises Crichton.

“The earlier you start saving a little bit every month or start investing that appropriately for the goals you have in mind, the greater the compounding return will be. Make sure that your money is put into a pot that is working hard towards your goals.”

News.title: Our holidays have become smartphone binges – here’s how we can truly relax
News.content:

I’m on a sunlounger having a conversation with myself. So far, we’ve discussed the weather (delightful but a little cloudy), the book I’m struggling with (a Polish novel a friend bought me), and my anxiety about the emails I haven’t replied to (there are hundreds). This is supposed to be a holiday, one I’ve waited months for, and yet I couldn’t feel less relaxed.

If anything, having spent the last two days alone in a remote French suburb – a tactic employed to help me decompress before some friends join me – my prone-to-overthinking brain feels more wired than ever, desperate for something to cling to that will propel it into a deep yet strangely comforting downward spiral.

In a world where everyone is always online, and our phones are practically attached to our bodies, it’s no wonder many of us struggle to switch off and decompress. According to recent research by Virgin Media O2, Britons are set to spend an average of four years and eight months of their lives using mobile phones unintentionally, wasting years of our lives in the process to... what? Watch videos of cats growling at tigers that were probably made by AI? Unless that’s just my algorithm.

open image in gallery Switching off: Ralph Fiennes and Dakota Johnson in Guadagnino’s acclaimed 2015 film ‘A Bigger Splash’ ( Studio Canal )

Meanwhile, according to research carried out by social travel company Flash Pack, 88 per cent of British travellers want to use their phones less on holiday, yet only 8 per cent of them actually manage to switch them off. I’m very guilty of this, and am always very good at finding reasons to switch my phone back on after I’ve turned it off and locked it in a drawer: what if there’s a natural disaster and I need to call my family? What if someone I love has had a sudden accident? What if my cat sitter needs to know where I keep the litter?

“We are in a constant state of psychological readiness, and our nervous system is at a state of heightened activation, which makes it difficult to relax,” explains psychotherapist Nino Sopromadze. “Our phones are extensions of us, which blurs the lines between work and rest. Our nervous system doesn’t get a clear signal that it’s safe to switch off, and it definitely isn’t designed to switch instantly from chronic alertness into deep relaxation.”

But not being able to relax is about more than suffering from a raging screentime addiction, one that, in my case, keeps me in a perpetual state of waiting for notifications. Because even when the phone is off and locked in a drawer, I still find it hard to be present. Instead of listening to the soothing sounds of the cicadas or feeling the warmth of the sun on my face, my mind is busy inventing reasons to panic: is that person who hasn’t replied to my WhatsApps secretly mad at me? Did I offend people when I made that dirty joke the other day? Do all my friends hate me? And so on.

This is mental noise, and isn’t supposed to get louder on holiday. But in the modern world, a holiday feels rarer than it perhaps once did. To those of us under pressure to make ends meet in the cost of living crisis, working multiple jobs and juggling various projects that often bleed into our evenings and weekends, allowing ourselves to just sit still for a bit is unfamiliar territory.

“Holidays give us something we’re not used to anymore: thinking time,” says Lee Thompson, co-founder of the travel brand, Flash Pack. “And thinking time can be your best friend or your worst enemy. You’re suddenly not busy, and your brain fills the gap. Realistically, it takes about three days to properly switch off. Your brain needs that long to stop performing and start resting, which is why a long weekend rarely does it.”

Try not to take a photo for the first 20-30 minutes after arriving somewhere new ... Give your brain a chance to absorb it first Sarah Hodges, Therapy Network Manager at Headspace

Part of the problem is the pressure we put on ourselves. We build holidays up like they’re going to magically cure all of our underlying stressors and then feel confused when that doesn’t happen the second we slather ourselves in SPF. “One of the biggest misconceptions about vacation is that we should feel relaxed the minute it begins,” says Sarah Hodges, Therapy Network Manager at Headspace. “Our nervous systems don’t work like a light switch; we need time to shift out of ‘doing” mode and into relaxation mode. Instead of rushing to fit everything in, take a walk, unpack, and simply let yourself arrive.”

There are more tangible things we can do, too, to help ground ourselves in the moment. Even if you can’t lock your phone in a drawer (this might actually make matters worse because suddenly it feels forbidden), you could rethink your holiday photography strategy, perhaps. “I would suggest delaying your first vacation photo,” adds Hodges. “Try not to take a photo for the first 20-30 minutes after arriving somewhere new. We often shift to document the moment before we give ourselves the opportunity to truly experience it. Give your brain a chance to absorb it first; you’ll often feel more grounded and present.”

Sartorially, there are tricks, too, that might help you to delineate between your holiday and non-holiday lives. I have a trunk full of summer clothes that I tend to only wheel out for holidays: sheer slip dresses I wouldn’t wear in London, co-ords I’ve worn to festivals, and oversized linen shirts I like to put over bikinis. “Wear something that is only for vacation, a favourite shirt, sandals, a specific hat you don’t wear at home,” suggests Hodges. “Our brains create strong associations, and those small cues help signal that it’s safe to slow down.”

Another useful tip can be to refrain from organising too many activities on your holiday, allowing for spontaneous plans that you can make based on how you’re feeling in the present moment as opposed to committing to something you inevitably wind up cancelling. “Don’t optimise the holiday,” says Sopromadze. “A packed itinerary is just work in a sun hat; be honest with yourself. Scheduling every minute can be a way to avoid rest. Let things unfold naturally; whether it leads to boredom or spontaneity, this is often where genuine rest begins.”

Taking rest seriously is not something that comes naturally to our culture. And as a freelancer, I’m as guilty of that as anyone, always finding an excuse to work instead of simply chilling out. But chill out we must, and not just for the obvious reasons. In her book Sacred Rest, Dr Saundra Dalton-Smith claims there are seven types of rest: physical, mental, spiritual, sensory, creative, emotional, and social. And we need all of them to thrive – a study conducted by UC San Francisco in 2024 found that deep rest can benefit our bodies on a cellular level, too, which can protect us against myriad diseases.

open image in gallery Focus on small changes – like setting aside a half-hour window to check your phone if you feel it’s impossible to go without it ( Pattarisara - stock.adobe.com )

“Taking time to relax can have a huge impact on both our physical and mental health, helping to reverse the impact of stressors,” says Rex Fan, lead behavioural insights specialist at Bupa UK Insurance. “Switching off can help improve your blood pressure, mood and sleep, which all contribute towards better physical health and better mood.”

Finally, if all of this feels like one step too far, remember it’s okay to take it slow. The last thing any of us needs is to get stressed about trying not to be stressed. “Aiming high with your switch-off goals might make it easier to fall at the first hurdle whilst you’re on holiday,” adds Fan. “Instead, it’s better to break down your behaviour, and focus on making smaller changes throughout your break. For example, instead of not checking your phone for the entire day, set time aside where you leave your phone out of sight for, say, 30 minutes or so.”

After about a week, I felt myself starting to properly relax into my holiday, which is how I ended up extending it by another week. By the end, I’d lost track of what day it was, living perpetually on Sunday time, which I think was a good sign. Still, it took much longer than I would’ve liked to get there. Practice makes perfect, they say, which is why I’m already researching my next holiday.

A class of proteins in the immune system could play a role in keeping some people safe from cancer despite lifelong exposure to risks, scientists say.

Humans have billions of different proteins in the body known as antibodies that are randomly produced by the immune system to bind to molecules found on bacteria, viruses, fungi, toxins or allergens.

Antibodies help the body fight off infections, either by marking pathogens for destruction by immune cells or directly neutralising them.

However, in some people, antibodies may mistakenly bind to normal molecules in their own body and cause their immune system to attack healthy cells and tissues.

Previous research has shown that these “autoantibodies”, or auto-Abs, can target molecules that the immune system uses to fight infectious diseases.

Such auto-Abs have also been linked to infectious diseases and inflammatory conditions.

open image in gallery Close up picture of woman lighting up a cigarette ( Alamy/PA )

Now, scientists suspect developing ways to control auto-Abs in cancer can help patients reduce their disease severity.

"There is ample evidence that the immune system plays a significant role in cancer," said Laurent Casanova, a professor in the Children's Medical Centre Research Institute at UT Southwestern (CRI).

"Our job will be to determine if there are auto-Abs that could offer protection against cancer or drive cancer outcomes,” Dr Casanova said.

Scientists have so far discovered auto-Abs that bind to about a dozen of the 50 or so known immune system molecules called cytokines.

The discoveries have led to treatment methods called immunotherapies, including the now popular checkpoint inhibitor drugs and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells.

These therapies have bolstered the theory that auto-Abs indeed influence cancer development and growth, explaining why some people remain cancer-free despite lifelong risks.

“Antibody repertoires, including autoantibodies targeting immune pathways, may shape cancer immunosurveillance,” scientists wrote.

open image in gallery Preventable cancer risk factors ( Cancer Research UK via Eurekalert )

In further studies, they hope to catalogue and study auto-Abs in a large and diverse group of volunteers.

The participants will include those with genetic syndromes or behaviours known to promote cancer, such as heavy smokers and ageing individuals, including centenarians.

By studying auto-Abs in these people, scientists hope to develop new ways to help patients reduce their cancer risk or treat existing disease more effectively.

“Mapping antibody landscapes across cancer-free, at-risk, and cancer-affected individuals could clarify their roles in cancer susceptibility and disease outcome,” they wrote in the journal Cell.

Researchers have also uncovered over 80 genes, which, when mutated, impair the body's ability to fight off infections like influenza and Covid-19, mirroring inborn immunity errors.

They hope to study these mutations further to understand the risks they pose to the development of cancer.

The detective who spearheaded the investigation into the death of Pc Andrew Harper says he is "appalled" that two men jailed over his manslaughter could qualify for early release.

Pc Harper died from fatal injuries in 2019 after becoming entangled in a strap trailing behind a car, which dragged him down a country lane in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, as his killers escaped a quad bike theft.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers might be freed halfway through their 13-year jail sentences under Government initiatives to ease severe prison overcrowding.

Detective Superintendent Stuart Blaik told the BBC he was “deeply concerned and appalled” by the prospect and that Cole and Bowers should “not be afforded the opportunity” of early release.

He said: “Neither of them showed any remorse during their time in police custody or during their subsequent trial.

“I hope the Government takes account of the strength of public feeling on this issue, which has been both clear and widespread,”

open image in gallery Jessie Cole (left) and Albert Bowers ( Thames Valley Police )

The Government has resisted pressure to exempt the two men from the early release scheme, part of the Sentencing Act passed earlier this year which cut the minimum amount of time many offenders would have to spend in prison.

Thames Valley Police Chief Constable Jason Hogg said he was receiving legal advice on whether the force could join a legal challenge mooted by local Police Federation chief Aileen O’Connor to prevent Cole and Bowers being freed.

The officer’s widow Lissie Harper said the Government “has punched us in the gut… they should be ashamed of themselves”.

“Hopefully we can make the current Government come to their senses and realise we cannot put people like this back on our streets.

“Justice should mean justice and serving the sentence given,” she said.

The Prime Minister has said he wanted to “go further” with the exemptions after ordering a review of the scheme, but this was “not possible without the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing”.

Those released will face tougher probation conditions, including electronic monitoring, random drug testing and possible bans from driving, pubs and events such as football matches.

The driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and will not be eligible for release under the scheme.

At least six people have been killed in a school shooting in Thailand, authorities said, with the victims including teachers and pupils.

The shooting happened at around 10am local time at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in the Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi province, located just outside Bangkok.

As the shooting unfolded, police urged people to hide and wait for the authorities, saying an active shooting incident was underway and that the attacker was believed to be inside a school computer room.

Thai police later said six victims had died and at least 15 were injured, including two who remain in critical condition. The suspected gunman died by suicide, Lt Col Dechrapee Kongdee, Nonthaburi ⁠Provincial Police Commander, told Reuters.

The shooter, who was a student of the school, also shot and killed his own grandparents at their home on Friday morning before attacking the school. He fired 26 rounds and another 34 rounds of ammunition were found at ‌the scene, ​police ‌said in a ⁠statement.

open image in gallery Students run as they evacuate from Debsirin Nonthaburi School, the site of a shooting incident, in Bang Kruai district ( Reuters )

A video, shared to the police’s Facebook handle, showed students crouching under desks inside a classroom as gunfire rang out in the background.

"Who is still stuck there? Hide securely," the police wrote on their Facebook page as the attack took place.

Pictures showed students running out of the school in panic as ambulances arrived on the scene. A picture also showed one person lying on a stretcher outside an ambulance while a medic attended to another person.

An 18-year-old student said he first thought firecrackers were going off or someone was banging an object.

open image in gallery A teacher reacts while embracing a person at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, the site of a shooting incident, in Bang Kruai district in Nonthaburi province on the outskirts of Bangkok ( Reuters )

"I didn't think it was a gun at first," ‌he told Reuters. "There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again."

The suspect, reportedly a ninth-grade student, barricaded himself on the third floor of the school's building, according to a local media report.

As the incident unfolded, police urged the public and media to stop livestreaming the incident and evacuated the teachers and students.

open image in gallery Students react with a relative after being evacuated from Debsirin Nonthaburi School, the site of a shooting incident, in Bang Kruai district in Nonthaburi province on the outskirts of Bangkok ( Reuters )

open image in gallery A schoolgirl cries outside her school where deaths and injuries were reported after a shooting in Thailand's Nonthaburi province, Friday ( AP )

Emergency worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith, 47, described arriving as ‌the shooting was ongoing and said his team treated students with injuries in the back, chest and arms.

They found a male teacher lying dead on an upper floor of the school, and in another room they found a female teacher with wounds to her chest and arm.

"We gave CPR for ⁠about 30 minutes and rushed her to the hospital as we could not get her heart rate up, but we tried our best," he said.

Friday’s incident is the second major school shooting in Thailand this year.

In February, a 17-year-old entered Patongprathankiriwat School in Hat Yai district, Songkhla province after stealing a firearm from a police officer.

The student shot at the school director and a female student, briefly taking several teachers and students hostage. The school director died, and the shooter was eventually detained by police.

Thailand has strict gun laws, with illegal possession of firearms punishable with up to 10 years in jail. However, the country is believed to have more than 10 million privately-owned guns in circulation, according to data by the University of Sydney’s School of Public Health – one of the highest gun ownership rates in the region.

News.content:

An American has been rescued from an Antarctic base to a New Zealand hospital in a rare midwinter rescue.

An aircraf flew from the Australian city of Hobart to the U.S. McMurdo Station in Antarctica on July 31 in response to an “urgent request for assistance”.

The jet landed after a five hour and 30 minute flight at the Phoenix Airfield near McMurdo in darkness and with temperatures as low as minus 43 C (minus 45.4 F), the statement said.

The American was flown on the same day to a hospital in Christchurch, New Zealand, as weather conditions at the Antarctic air strip worsened, said Skytraders, which is contracted by the Australian Antarctic Program.

The U.S. National Science Foundation told the Australian Broadcasting Corp. that the patient was admitted to the Christchurch Hospital in a “serious condition.”

New Zealand’s Health Ministry on Friday would not comment on the American’s condition or say whether the American remained in hospital.

The mission’s copilot, Louise Robertson, said conditions were close to the limit of the aircraft’s capabilities.

open image in gallery A sign is photographed at McMurdo Station, a United States Antarctic research station, on Dec. 4, 2018. (National Science Foundation via AP, File) ( U.S. National Science Foundation )

“We had some what’s called nautical twilight, which is a very minimal amount of light that is pretty much pitch blackness and also the extreme cold temperatures. We are right on the verge of the limitation of the aircraft,” Robertson told ABC.

“It was very close to being too cold,” she said.” It got down to minus 43 (Celsius), which is the coldest I’ve ever felt. It was about 8 knots of wind, so quite a bit of wind-chill as well.”

Robertson said plans to fly to the base on the Ross Ice Shelf a day earlier were aborted due to a snow storm.

“There … was really just such a narrow window of opportunity,” Robertson said.

“To get there in complete darkness in these extreme cold temperatures is very, very rare. I believe it hasn’t been done before,” she added.

The sun last set at the geographic South Pole on March 23 and will not rise until Sept. 21.

The New Zealand Air Force evacuated a New Zealand citizen working on the U.S. Antarctic Program from the Phoenix Airfield in a C-130 Hercules in a medical emergency in April, which is the Southern Hemisphere autumn.

In August last year, the final month of the Southern Hemisphere winter, New Zealand used the same type of four-engine turboprop transport aircraft to evacuate three people on a flight from McMurdo for medical treatment.

News.content:

As well as a good brain, students heading to university this autumn need a healthy bank account to help them through their degree course.

Fortunately, there are plenty of student bank accounts available, and it’s crucial that young people choose the best one for them, rather than just sticking with their old bank or choosing their parents’ bank because it’s an easy option. In the latest Student Banking Survey by the student finance website Save the Student, 40% of those surveyed chose their student account because it was with the bank they were already with, while 30% followed friends or family recommendations, and 28% were swayed by freebies.

“Some of these motives have more merit than others, but ultimately, none should be as important as the interest-free overdraft that comes with a student bank account,” says Tom Allingham, student bank accounts expert at Save the Student.

“Opening a student bank account is one of the most important things anyone can do to give their finances a strong foundation at university. Picking the right account could even be the difference between making it through uni or not.”

The reason picking the right student bank account is so important is because students are finding it harder than ever to make ends meet – the latest Save Our Student National Student Money Survey found student maintenance loans fall short of living costs by an average of £502 per month.

“Students have a lot of work to do to cover their expenses,” warns Allingham. “Making ends meet at uni has never been tougher.”

Here, Allingham and Alicia Hempstead, personal finance and insurance expert at MoneySuperMarket, outline everything students – and parents – should know about choosing a student bank account…

Be aware of eligibility requirementsBefore considering the financial implications of the bank account they choose, students need to be sure they’re actually eligible to open one of the accounts.

Get a free fractional share worth up to £100.

Capital at risk. Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

Get a free fractional share worth up to £100.

Capital at risk. Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

Hempstead says you need to be 18 or over and have an offer for a qualifying full-time course at a UK university to open a student bank account.

“While part-time or postgraduate students may still be able to apply, some student bank accounts are only available to students on qualifying full-time courses, so it’s important to check the requirements before signing up,” she says.

Consider overdraft amounts

Every bank offers an interest-free overdraft with a student bank account, with all giving students at least a year after graduation to repay it on the same 0% terms, says Allingham.

“But how much you get and how likely you are to receive it can vary massively,” he warns. “This year, the interest-free allowances range from £1,500 to over £3,250 – although the limit in your first year will generally be lower than the advertised maximum.

“What’s more, while some banks will guarantee the size of their overdraft, others will say theirs is ‘up to’ a certain amount. In other words, you may have to choose between one bank offering a lower, guaranteed amount, or another offering a larger potential figure.”

Don’t forget overdraft terms

Hempstead points out that as well as the size of the arranged overdraft and whether it’s interest-free, what happens if you exceed the agreed overdraft limit can also vary.

“Therefore, before signing up for a student bank account, it’s important to check the small print. If students misuse their interest-free overdraft, it could lead to extra debt which may harm their credit rating.”

Graduate options

Towards the end of their time at university it’s worth students looking at what their account offers after graduation, and Hempstead says: “Some banks allow students to switch to a graduate account with a reduced interest-free overdraft period after they graduate, giving them more time to repay what they owe.”

Perks and rewards

Many student bank accounts offer incentives such as free railcards, cashback, and discounts at popular shops, which can help students’ money go further.

“While discounts and perks are offered as an incentive, they shouldn’t outweigh features like an interest-free overdraft,” Hempstead points out.

And Allingham adds: “If and when a rainy day hits, having a larger interest-free overdraft will be far more useful than a £100 sign-up freebie, or having stayed loyal to a bank you were already with.

“And compared to other forms of borrowing, it’s easily the safest and cheapest form of emergency cash. Ultimately, it’s better to have it and not need it, than need it and not have it.”Hempstead says some student bank accounts offer access to financial planning and money-management advice tailored for students.

Don’t forget it can affect your credit score

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

Having a student account can help students gain experience managing day-to-day finances and borrowing responsibly, Hempstead points out.

But it’s wise to use it responsibly, she warns.

“While a student bank account won’t automatically build a student’s credit score, using an arranged overdraft responsibly, staying within agreed limits, and making repayments on time can contribute to a positive credit history,” she says.

“This may make it easier for students to apply for credit cards, mortgages, and loans in the future, although lenders will consider a range of factors when assessing applicants.”

Look at the reviewsAllingham says it’s important for students to look at the reviews of each lender too. There are many best student bank account lists on the internet, including those compiled by Save the Student, MoneySaving Expert and MoneySuperMarket.

“We include a ‘student satisfaction’ score for each provider in our list of the best student bank accounts, sourced from our survey,” says Allingham.

“If a bank has a high score, it might suggest that their customer service is good, or that they’re pretty reliable at approving requests for a larger overdraft.”

News.title: Elderflower cordial, rust remover and sink unblocker: The clever uses of citric acid
News.content:
Citric acid has long been a favourite for descaling kettles and coffee machines, but its uses extend far beyond banishing limescale.

After Sarah-Jane Hoadley shared her top cleaning jobs for citric acid, readers flooded the comments with their own tips. They revealed just how versatile this inexpensive household staple can be, whether that’s using the powdered form, or lemons, in which it occurs naturally.

From removing rust from tools to unblocking sinks and even making homemade elderflower cordial, here’s what our readers had to say.

A cleaner barbecue

With barbecue season well underway, reader Tom Spencer tells us about his top tip.

“Cleaning with lemons is all over the internet nowadays,” he says. “I use cut lemons or limes to clean the barbecue grates after scraping with the wire scraper once at a high temperature. It is as simple as rubbing the halved lemon onto the bars. The acid does the rest, and gets any little bits off. Then put olive oil onto some kitchen roll and rub the bars so the food doesn’t stick.”

Summer drinks

Speaking of summer, citric acid can also be used in various cocktail, cordial and wine recipes, as detailed by Janet Adams, 74, from Scotland.

“I bought the citric acid last year to make elderflower wine. I was somewhat nervous about putting it in, acid after all,” she says. Janet has a host of self-seeded elder trees on the land where she lives. “Last year was the first time I put them to any use.”

When making cordial, the flower heads have to be picked on a hot day when the perfume is strong. They do get soaked overnight, but “be careful to allow anything crawly to escape before that”, Janet adds.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Mo Salah ‘set to be reunited with Liverpool flop’ as Trabzonspor working on transfer for £400k-a-week striker
Sports.content:
MO SALAH could be joined by a familiar face at Trabzonspor with the Turkish club reportedly working on another ambitious deal.

Salah, 34, penned a two-year contract worth about £360,000 a week to join the side that finished third in the Turkish Super Lig last season.



And the challengers’ spending spree looks set to continue.

According to The i Paper, Trabzonspor are keen to reunite Salah with his ex-Liverpool team-mate, Darwin Nunez.



The Uruguayan earns about £400,000 a week at Al-Hilal but was chucked out of their Saudi Pro League squad when Karim Benzema joined in February.

Nunez, 27, was only eligible to play in the AFC Champions League Elite from then on, and he finished the campaign with a modest nine goals in 24 games.



Reports in Turkey state that Trabzonspor are ‘increasing the pressure’ in their pursuit of the centre-forward.

Al-Hilal, who splashed £46million on Nunez last year, could let him go for as little as £17m.

Tottenham have also been keeping tabs on the cut-price star but have not made a formal offer.

Nunez failed to catch fire at Liverpool, scoring just 40 goals in 143 games after what was then a club-record £85m move from Benfica in 2022.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But at that point he was one of the hottest properties on the market following a 34-goal campaign in Portugal.

Nunez spent three years as Salah’s team-mate and could become one of a few figures recognisable to Premier League fans in the Trabzonspor ranks.

Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana has joined on a second season-long loan, while ex-Manchester City defender Stefan Savic and former Evertonian John Lundstram have both played for the Trabzon side since 2024.

Ex-Southampton giant Paul Onuachu was the joint top scorer in the league last season with 22 goals but risks being frozen out at Trabzonspor if Nunez takes his place up top.

Sports.title: ‘Never heard a bigger load of rubbish’ – Ex-British tennis No1 slams Man Utd legend Paul Scholes in scathing rant
Sports.content:
GREG RUSEDSKI slammed Paul Scholes in a scathing rant – then challenged him to a game of tennis.

The former British No1 even hit out at the ex-Manchester United midfielder’s take as the “biggest load of rubbish in my life”.



Scholes, 51, ruffled his feathers during an episode of The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast with co-hosts Paddy McGuinness and Nicky Butt.

During the show, he claimed football is a more physically demanding sport than tennis.



Scholes – who played 718 times for the Red Devils between 1994 and 2013 – moaned about tennis: “Every two minutes you go and have your nice little glass of orange juice.

“You can play it when you’re 50, tennis. Play it when you’re 70, tennis.”

Then he added: “Football is much more demanding than tennis.”

But Rusedski was having none of it.

The Canada-born tennis star, winner of 15 career titles and former world No4, fired back in a brutal response.

And now he wants Scholes to walk the walk after talking the talk.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Rusedski, 52, told talkSPORT: “You can’t compare football to tennis. There’s no question about it.

“I was watching Paul Scholes saying, ‘Oh, football’s so much harder than tennis.’

“I’ve never heard a bigger load of rubbish in my life.

“Come on, Scholesy, let’s go play some tennis and see how long you can last out there.



“Having to move directions, no substitutions.

“There is no question, physically, tennis is much more demanding.

“With the travel schedule, with competing, with having to support and fund your own team.

“There are so many more things that make tennis a much more difficult sport.”

Sports.title: Rodri WANTS to join Barcelona in major blow to new Man City boss Enzo Maresca with Real Madrid missing out on Spain star
Sports.content:
RODRI wants to join Barcelona in a transfer blow for new Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca.

Spain’s World Cup winning captain is keen on a move back to his homeland after seven years at the Etihad.



And Barca are in pole position to beat Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid for the midfield maestro.

Rodri, 30, is in the final year of his City contract with no sign he is ready to extend his current deal.



Real, who have agreed a £115.8million deal with RB Leipzig for Yan Diomande, 19, were willing to pay £43m for Rodri’s signature.

But no agreement has materialised and Barca have stepped up their interest.



Barca midfielder Frenkie de Jong is expected to be out of action for a lengthy period after a medial knee ligament tear.

And a move to the Nou Camp would appeal to midfield ace Rodri given the bad blood he has with Real from when he won the Ballon d’Or in autumn 2024.

City, managed by Maresca after the Italian replaced Pep Guardiola this summer, had to give careful consideration to their own contract offer to Rodri – given the fact the defensive midfielder missed much of the last two years due to injury.

England midfielder Elliot Anderson has arrived for £116m but City could yet go to sign a replacement for Rodri if he leaves.

Morocco’s World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi is keen on a move from Lille to City although the French club are holding out for around £85m.

Meanwhile, winger Jeremy Doku has become the latest player to commit his long-term future to City.

The Belgium international has penned a five-year deal which will keep him at the Etihad until 2031 with the option of a further year.

Phil Foden, Abdukodir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol have already given new boss Enzo Maresca a boost by signing up for the long-term.

And Doku’s contract is expected to be officially confirmed when he returns to training at the City Football Academy next week.



The 24-year-old has become one of the most dangerous wide men in the Prem since arriving from Rennes in a £55 million deal three years ago.

His game developed under Pep Guardiola’s coaching and he was a key player last year as City won the domestic cup double.

Maresca is expected to rely heavily on getting the ball to wingers in his first season in charge so Doku is likely to be an integral part of his plans.



City could look to the transfer market if the likes of Rodri and Savinho depart.

However they are in no rush to do more business in the current window.

As well as the record signing of Anderson, they signed Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi in January and believe their recruitment has been strong this year.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced into tense reunion with £325,000-a-week Rashford… but if anyone can make it work, it’s Carrick
Sports.content:
THERE is usually great fanfare when a prodigal son returns home.

You think of the excitement among Tottenham fans as Gareth Bale rejoined from Real Madrid in 2020, or when Wayne Rooney made his Everton comeback at Goodison Park after 13 years away.



It’s fair to say Marcus Rashford’s unlikely return to Old Trafford has an altogether different vibe.

Because 18 months ago the prospect of a reunion with Manchester United looked about as likely as taking the eggs out of a baked cake.



And to be honest, he seemed pretty relieved about that.

By the time he was packed off to Aston Villa in February last year, his relationship with then-manager Ruben Amorim had not so much soured as rotted to the core.



He was snubbed by the Portuguese, who claimed Rashford’s attitude was so poor that he would rather select his 63-year-old goalkeeping coach Jorge Vital as a United sub.

It was quite a fall from grace for the England star, whose reputation had been near impeccable to that point.

But he answered the criticism with good performances on loan at Villa and Barcelona.

His exit at Old Trafford looked so set in stone that he had no qualms handing over his No 10 shirt to Matheus Cunha last summer.

And yet it is looking increasingly likely he will be back this season, meaning the United board find themselves in a very awkward position.

Because it wasn’t as straightforward as Amorim forcing him out — the club wanted him gone and his huge wages off their books.

He signed his mammoth £325,000-a-week contract, making him the club’s top earner, off the back of a stunning 2022-23 season when he netted 17 goals in the Premier League and looked right back to his best.

The Red Devils gave him the new deal a year before Sir Jim Ratcliffe purchased his stake in the club and took control of footballing operations.

The billionaire immediately went about making himself the most unpopular man in Manchester by making savage cuts, with hundreds of staff members made redundant.



Clearly, Ratcliffe and his new board resented the amount of money that Rashford was on from the very start, and they made it pretty obvious they were going to try to get rid at the first opportunity.

It was even leaked to the media by the club in the weeks before he left for Villa that every United manager had had issues with Rashford, not just Amorim.

When you have grown up in Manchester, supported United all your life and been in the academy since the age of seven, it’s not a huge surprise he was left bruised and disillusioned.

We saw something similar play out last year with captain Bruno Fernandes, the club’s second-highest earner, who went on the record saying the club wanted him gone.



Now, with a move to another side looking increasingly unlikely, the board are going to have to spin it back and say it was Amorim who wanted Rashford gone. Nothing to do with us, guv.

It all sets the stage for a potentially tense reunion — but the reason it could work is the man in the dugout.

Since Michael Carrick took over in January, the entire mood around United has shifted.

He immediately made Fernandes feel appreciated and he went on to produce one of the best second halves to a season in Prem history.

If anyone has the empathy, skills, and respect of his players, to rebuild the bridges burnt by Amorim and the board, it’s Carrick. He’s shown he can do it already.



There is little doubt Rashford, 28, is still a hugely talented player and, when he’s on song, he has a lot to offer at the highest level.

So the United hierarchy doesn’t have much choice but to put the politics of the last couple of difficult years aside and try to reintegrate him.

Luckily, they have the right man in charge to do it.



No Vin situation

Sorry to break it to Arsenal fans, but there wasn’t a chance in hell you were signing Vinicius Jr.

It was pretty clear from the off, especially for a cynic like me, that the Gunners were being used so the Brazilian could negotiate a pay rise at Real Madrid.

So it has come to pass, with him reportedly agreeing a brand spanking new contract at the Bernabeu.

It would have been the shock of the century had he not stayed at Real.

The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle should soften the blow for Arsenal.



But if their listless pre-season defeat by Real Betis is any guide, they still have work to do this transfer window.

Marc on the world stage

Being knocked out by the Argies in the World Cup semi-final was a very bitter pill to swallow for every England fan.

But we can at least console ourselves with the knowledge that we, as a country, are living rent-free in their heads.



The Argentine FA has announced July 15 will become ‘National Football Teams Day’, to commemorate their victory in Atlanta.

Not only did they embarrass themselves on the pitch in the final defeat by Spain, they’re now embarrassing themselves off it.

Big jump in prices

One of the most dispiriting aspects of Jumps racing — a sport millions of us love — is that the same faces seem to win everything.

If it’s not Willie Mullins or Gordon Elliott in Ireland, it’s Dan Skelton in England — and our reigning champion trainer continues to get stronger.

All-conquering owner JP McManus this week sent Skelton a new batch of future stars, including a £428,000 buy called Walkonseas.

Smaller owners and trainers are being priced out nowadays as the rich keep getting richer.

It means fewer and fewer yards can compete — and the game is all the poorer for it.

Sports.title: ‘It’s tough’ – Matthias Jaissle breaks silence on Guimaraes’ Arsenal transfer but insists Newcastle have ‘no excuses’
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE has “no excuse” not to bring success back to Newcastle despite the exodus of star names.

The German, 38, officially took charge on Wednesday – the same day a £75million fee was agreed with Arsenal for skipper Bruno Guimaraes – after arriving from Ah-Ahli in Saudi Arabia.



The Brazilian is the third big name departure after Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, though club chiefs are adamant Lewis Hall will not follow them despite Manchester United’s interest.

Jaissle said: “We lost a couple of really important players, but that’s also a chance.



“You can see it in a negative way, that there’s a lot of challenges and we can search for excuses, but that’s not our idea. We see the chance in these things.

“Give me a bit of time to really get to know the players, work with them. That’s the most important thing.

“We have a clear vision of where we want to go, and we want to be successful – of course, everyone wants to be that.

“It’s about hard work now in the pre-season and making progress.”

Newcastle have brought in a host of exciting young talents to replace the big hitters – but some are tipping Toon to be battling down the bottom rather than challenging at the top.

Even legendary record scorer Alan Shearer admits it will be a “challenge” for the new man following a bruising summer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Jaissle added: “I didn’t hear the talk (about relegation) because I try to avoid reading these things. I’ve mentioned it a couple of times but this is the challenge.

“There are so many transitions at the moment, many players left, big, big players, legends for the club left.

“But we need to see it as a chance, not having too many excuses now, just thinking forward (of) what we can influence.

“Control the controllables, I used to say, and we are sure there will be progress.”



Jaissle has been with his squad in La Manga since Saturday but admitted he had no involvement in the decision to sell Guimaraes.

Though he says fans can expect some incomings to fill the huge voids left.

He revealed: “One day I met him [Guimaraes] quickly, but the decision was already made.

“It was a nice conversation, a fantastic player, but also a great human being.

“It’s tough, but for him also the next challenge, and we need to deal with it at a later stage.



“We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes.

“I have some clear ideas but I want to give the players who are here a chance. They can show up. It is a new challenge for them and we can wait.

“We have, for sure, the capacity to do something on the market and our sporting director is aware of that.

“Then for sure when the season starts we will see some more new faces.”

Sports.title: Man Utd icon Nicky Butt BANNED from local tip after ‘raging’ row with staff
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER United great Nicky Butt claims he has been banned from his local tip after a row with staff.

Butt, 51, was “raging” when his Range Rover was deemed to be a commercial vehicle as the seats were down.



But the former midfielder went ahead and dumped his “smelly bags” at the centre near his home in Cheshire, chased by an attendant with a walkie-talkie.

He said: “There’s this guy at the gate bit, and he flags me down and goes, ‘Put your windows down I need to look in the back of your car’. I’m going, ‘What for?’.”



The Class of 92 hero continued: “I’ve got a lot of crap from the house, bit of cardboard . . . I missed the bin man last week, so I’ve got a few smelly bags. So I put the windows down, obviously my seats were down and apparently I’m not going in because it’s a commercial van. So I’m raging, literally.

“I’m putting a bit of cardboard in the tip.”



Butt then claimed the attendant accused him of trying to sneak in items.

The dad of two told The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast: “He said to me, ‘Your windows are blacked out because you’re sneaking stuff into it, into the tip’. And I went, ‘No, it’s standard, mate’.”

He then decided to drive into the site, believed to be the Woodhouse Lane Recycling Centre in Altrincham.

He said: “I thought, well, I’m there now, I’m gonna go for it. So I’ve got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up . . . trying to chase me up the hill, but he’s got his walkie-talkie out.



“So I’ve literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I’m going back down the hill, and he’s going mad at me. Anyway, I’m banned from the tip.”

Butt won six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the Champions League with United before moving to Newcastle in 2004.

He then finished playing in China, and was CEO of League Two side Salford until quitting in 2024.



The Sun contacted him for comment.

Sports.title: World Cup team ‘suddenly’ paid by Fifa after EIGHT MONTHS of asking – days after accusing Infantino of ‘blackmail’
Sports.content:
JORDAN have suddenly received all of the money owed by Fifa after an eight-month wait.

The drama came as the funds arrived just TWO days after their FA chief accused the governing body of “blackmail”.



Prince Ali bin Al Hussein confirmed on X that the outstanding bonuses from December’s Fifa Arab Cup had finally been paid on Thursday morning.

The Jordan FA president thanked Fifa for delivering the cash owed to the national team’s players and coaching staff.



He stressed that the payment had arrived nearly a year after Jordan reached the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

But Prince Ali insisted the development would not change his stance on the controversial Fifa president Gianni Infantino.



He said: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa.

“My FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

The dramatic payment came just 48 hours after Prince Ali launched a blistering attack on Fifa and claimed Jordan had been pressured to back Infantino.

He alleged that during this summer’s World Cup he was verbally told endorsing the Swiss chief would “go a long way” towards helping his cash-strapped association.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Jordan had been waiting since December for the prize money earned by reaching the Arab Cup final, despite repeatedly asking for the funds.

Prince Ali also criticised the difficulties facing his country during their first World Cup.



That included supporters being denied US visas, expensive tickets and tax costs for players and staff.

Infantino, 56, is fighting to retain control after abandoning his controversial plan to allow private investors to buy a stake in the World Cup enterprise.

But he vowed to remain in office, while the FA, Welsh FA and Uefa have withdrawn their support ahead of next year’s presidential election.

In the X post, he wrote: “Thank you to the Fifa administration for suddenly this morning delivering what was owed to our players and coaching staff, for the Jordan National team’s accession to the final of the Fifa Arab Cup in Qatar last December.

“This was funding that should have been received eight months ago.



“While this is a good development for our players, it does not change the serious concerns we in the football world have regarding the Fifa leadership.

“Nor does it change what our FAs have been subjected to in the past.

“It is symptomatic of those exact difficulties that we all face, and that are usually linked to the Fifa presidential elections.

“And it does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa.

“My FA will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”



At the 2026 Fifa World Cup, Jordan did not manage to overcome any of their three opponents – Argentina, Algeria, and Austria – in Group J.

Sports.title: New Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle denies CHAOS at club after big-name exits as he repeats key word five times
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have endured a summer of chaos with three star players and the manager out of the door.

But if the exodus has left the Toon Army fearing the worst, the buzzword within the club is “transition”.



New boss Matthias Jaissle used it five times in a ten-minute interview with the media in La Manga – after firstly refusing to use the recent big-name exits as an excuse not to succeed.

Fresh from losing captain Bruno Guimaraes, as well as the departures of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, Eddie Howe’s replacement Jaissle was ice cool as he sat on a stool in a La Manga club house to answer questions.



The 38-year-old German faces a baptism of fire and has his work cut out to get Newcastle into shape in time for the Premier League season opener against Liverpool in 16 days time.

But while Howe no longer had the energy for the fight anymore, Jaissle had no doubt in the sweltering 34C heat he would have his squad ready for the Reds.



He said: “I’m confident to do the best out of that short amount of time.

“Of course it’s another challenge, because there’s not too many days left until the first match against Liverpool, but that’s now the phase.

“You cannot change anything, I cannot ask the squad director to turn the time back again.

“So, again, all together, the whole staff, we tried to encourage them in the first meeting already, that now it’s even more important that everyone raises the standards, and the same we expect from the players, to find that unity and that DNA of how we want to play football already in the first match.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Toon’s performance director James Bunce described the short turnaround to install the new man’s ideas as “speed dating with no time to waste”.

But no matter what work goes on, many feel Howe hit the glass ceiling by lifting the Carabao Cup and qualifying for the Champions League in 2025, especially given the financial handcuffs imposed by SCR rules.

It has forced Toon into flogging several star names. Recruitment has focused on bringing in a host of promising, though some unproven, prodigies to bolster the ranks.



From the outside looking in, the glory days appear to be way off. But Jaissle, despite his tender years, says leading a young team to the top is his speciality.

He said: “It was a really, really successful story under Eddie. There’s huge respect for what he was building and now there are many, many changes. But, that’s a chance and we want to build on that chance and start growing.

“In Salzburg I had a couple of challenges but we were so successful. Then in Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia, I took over a club that was just promoted and we were also quite successful there.

“So I can manage when there are a lot of challenges within the club and the transition and working with young players. This is the approach and also why I’m here now.”

Jaissle does arrive with silverware on his CV. He won the double in his first season at Salzburg and retained the league the next while reaching the Champions League knockouts.



Two years later he helped transform Al-Ahli into one of Asia’s top sides, leading them to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns and a Saudi Super Cup.

Managing in the Premier League against some of the game’s greatest coaches is a whole different ball game.

And trophies are very much on the agenda on Tyneside.

He said: “This is something I don’t have on my CV, but that’s normal in football. At one point it has to be your first step and I’m now at that moment after being successful in Saudi Arabia and Austria. Everyone was dreaming about being a part of the Premier League and now here we are.

“I have always big ambitions. That’s the key element for every coach, otherwise I would be not here.



“That’s the same here now in Newcastle, but it’s always easy saying where we want to go and on which place we want to end up. For me, it doesn’t make too much sense in football because it’s difficult to plan things in advance.

EDDIE HOWE'S RECORD AT NEWCASTLE EDDIE HOWE will forever be a Newcastle legend after leading the Toon to their first trophy in 70 years. But that Carabao Cup win, and two Champions League qualifications, weren’t enough to keep everyone happy on Tyneside. Here is Howe’s Newcastle record: Premier League 2021-22 – 11th (19th when he took over) 2022-23 – 4th 2023-24 – 7th 2024-25 – 5th 2025-26 – 12th Trophies won Carabao Cup 2024-25

“As you probably know, therefore, it’s for me the most important thing that you just do your best every day and get the best out of the players, try to improve them, support them, give them also the courage to grow, and that’s now the phase where we’re in in the pre-season, and therefore I’m really much looking forward.”

Both a member of the Saudi Public Investment Fund, who own 80 per cent of the club, and Jamie Reuben, who owns the rest, were on camp at the Hotel Grand Hyatt La Manga Club.

Newcastle CEO David Hopkinson, whose aim is to be “in the debate about being the top club in the world” by 2030, and sporting director Ross Wilson were too.



They all want a return on the £9.5m compensation fee paid for Jaissle. But with such a young squad, the Toon Army may be in for a few more rough moments before the Mags are flying high again.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But bullish Jaissle, who used the magic word one final time, cannot wait to get going.

Jaissle added: “This is now a transition phase, but I’m really excited now to finally officially be here in the camp already. I’m even more looking forward to seeing them back home in Newcastle and start that journey.”

Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future

Real Madrid were long considered the favourites to sign Rodri before Barcelona entered the running, with the midfielder having entered the final 12 months of his contract at Manchester City

Rodri's agent has announced that the Manchester City star wants to join Barcelona over arch rivals Real Madrid. Rodri, 30, agreed personal terms with Barca on Thursday in a sudden and dramatic twist.

‌



The Spaniard had been in talks with Real for weeks after suggesting back in March that he was keen on a move to the Bernabeu. But Barcelona have hijacked the move after Rodri spoke to their manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director Deco and was convinced to join the La Liga champions.

‌



Although City haven't given up hope of tying Rodri down to a new contract after he entered the final year of his current deal, Etihad chiefs are well aware of his desire to return to Spain. In a late-night interview with Cadena SER, Rodri's agent, Pablo Barquero, revealed all.

‌



"Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Barquero told the Spanish radio station.

Sports.title: Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has split world football this summer, with football associations sharing statements about his premiership, with Argentina and England again at odds

View Image Lionel Messi's Argentina have backed FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

The Argentine Football Association have shared a statement in support of FIFA president Gianni Infantino's premiership over the last decade. That stance is at odds with the Football Association, who are withdrawing its support for his re-election, much like the Football Association of Wales.

‌



The AFA statement, translated into English from Spanish, reads: "Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model. stable and transparent.

‌



"In this sense, in relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the Administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties.

‌



"That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of FIFA. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between FIFA, its member associations and the confederations.

"In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of FIFA, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

‌



"From our point of view, this transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practice our beloved sport.

"Accordingly, with the upcoming FIFA Congress approaching, the Association that I proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football."

Turning to midfield, Scholes felt Manuel Ugarte would depart and the Uruguayan was linked with a move before picking up an injury at the World Cup. Mason Mount also featured on Scholes' eight-man list, though the England international has caught the eye during pre-season.

‌



Additionally, Scholes felt the moment had arrived to say goodbye to Harry Maguire, who continues to have a key role at United. He said: "I'm thinking about a Manchester United team you want to win the league and the Champions League and that's where United should be aiming. I'm not sure you'd do that with Maguire."

He was equally prepared to let Patrick Dorgu leave.
