Meanwhile, James Trafford sealed a club-record move to Leeds after completing a medical at Elland Road. Leeds have agreed a £40m fee plus add-ons with City for the 23-year-old, who will become the world’s fourth most expensive goalkeeper.

Sports.title: Alessia Russo: ‘When you join the club, you take on a part of Arsenal and the love’
Sports.content:
Arms hooked over the bar at the front of the bus, sunglasses on, a drink in one hand and the other pointed towards the fans as she moved to the music and joined in with the singing and chanting, Alessia Russo was having a blast.

“I had the time of my life that day,” says the Arsenal forward of the 9km parade through the red smoke-filled streets of north London after Arsenal men’s Premier League triumph and Arsenal women’s Champions Cup success.

It has been a running joke among fans to refer to the 27-year-old as a “childhood Gooner”, which was turbo-charged when the shirt a very small Russo was wearing in a family photo with the FA Cup was changed from a Manchester United one into an Arsenal one.

While she was not a childhood Gooner, she is fast becoming an adult one.

“Since I’ve joined the club and seen the people around the place, it’s impossible to not become a part of Arsenal and to feel like I support Arsenal,” she says. “I want them to do well, I’m backing them every way, and the parade was just one of the most amazing things I’ve experienced. The fans, the atmosphere, celebrating the men winning the Prem, something they’d worked so hard for for so many years, I was just soaking it in, having fun and enjoying myself.

“It was just a really, really special day. It was nice to experience it with Lotte [Wubben-Moy] and Leah [Williamson] who are proper Gooners, but when you come to Arsenal you take on a part of it and start to understand and absorb their love for Arsenal. I definitely feel that and it’s nice to feel like you’re a part of something like that.

“You pick out moments where you win trophies as the main ones that stand out within your career, but that will definitely always stand out for me.”

There were people everywhere, on every balcony, rooftop, bollard and traffic light, of all ages, races and religions. Young boys, but also, in contrast to the Arsenal parades of the 90s and noughties, so many young girls. Cultivating and supporting that fresh generation interested in watching and playing the game is something Russo is passionate about.

View image in fullscreen Top: Arsenal go past fans with the Women’s Champions Cup trophy in May.

Photograph: Steven Paston/PA

Above: Fans celebrate Arsenal men’s and women’s success during the club’s victory parade.

Photograph: Aldo Ciarrocchi/Alamy

That is the reason she launched her own foundation this year and why she helped launch the fifth year of Starling Bank’s Kick On initiative. This partners local businesses with girls’ teams in need of sponsorship and subsidises the front-of-shirt sponsorship.

Starling commissioned surveys of 1,000 adult female players, 1,010 11-17 female players, 501 small- and medium-sized business leaders and 1,092 grassroots football coaches. Nearly every grassroots female football club (97%) said their team needed more funds, with opportunities for girls suffering as a result. The surveys found 76% of female players said they will have to drop out of their team or the sport altogether if more funding is not secured in the next five years, and 40% of female players said their team does not receive the same amount of funding as men’s teams.

“They are quite damning statistics, which is such a shame considering the growth we see in the women’s game,” says Russo. “Over the past five or six years, the growth has just been incredible, but there’s still work to do at the bottom to build it up.”

The risk is that women’s football loses momentum and fails to attract potential star players into the pathway. “I always say you never want to miss out on the next Leah Williamson or Lotte Wubben-Moy, you don’t want to miss out on talented young players just because they haven’t got a local team, or the team that they were at folds,” Russo says. “It seems like such an easy fix as teams don’t need much, but obviously it isn’t because it’s still a problem.

“I look back on all the people I met through my grassroots journey and every single one of them played a part in my career and I’m still friends with many of them. If local businesses can invest in one team, you never know, you might help produce a superstar who goes on to have an incredible career who will always remember you being a part of it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Russo scored key goals in Champions League last season, including against Chelsea. Photograph: Harvey Murphy/News Images/Alamy

“There’s more to it than just investment, it’s that you can have a say in a core part of these young girls’ journeys and lives.”

With no major international women’s tournament, Russo has enjoyed a rare summer off and she has had the chance to focus on the broader issues she is passionate about, as well as some much-needed rest.

“It was important I did have some proper downtime,” she says. “Over the past few years, the minutes and tournaments have increased, so I needed to look after my body and get myself in a good place mentally. I shut down for about two and a half weeks and just enjoyed time with friends and family, which was lovely, but by the end of it I was ready to start exercising again, I didn’t know what to do with myself.

“I quite enjoy training on my own over the summer, you get to know your best routines and habits. I often go on holiday with my family and train out there, which is nice because everyone wants to get involved.

“I just took time for myself too, being a normal 27-year-old girl, going on holidays. I went to the England v Panama game in New York and got to be a fan and be around that buzz of the World Cup. I had Toonie’s [England teammate Ella Toone] hen do and wedding, which was amazing.”

View image in fullscreen After a few months off, Russo is back at Arsenal for pre-season training. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Russo had a standout year in 2025-26; many believe her game moved up a level for club and country. “I’m pleased with my season for Arsenal and England from a personal point of view, but, ultimately, I’ll always judge it on the trophies we win,” she says.

“We’ve learned a lot as a team over the past couple of years at Arsenal, but are hungry for the new season. We’ve made it quite clear we want to do everything we can to be the team most capable of winning the WSL and Renée [Slegers, the coach] has set the standard high this pre-season.

“We’ve got seven new players, we’ve got a squad that’s raring to go, the competition in it is high. I feel happy, but now I want to continue to push on with Arsenal and England and win some trophies.”

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah to earn upwards of £14.5m per season in two-year Trabzonspor deal
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor and the Egypt forward will receive €17m (£14.5m) a season.

The ⁠announcement to ‌the Turkish stock ‌exchange came ​as Trabzonspor fans prepared to head to the club’s stadium for a ceremony to mark the 34-year-old’s former Liverpool player’s signing on a free transfer the day after ⁠Salah arrived in Istanbul in the team’s kit.

Thousands of supporters cheered in Trabzonspor’s stadium, waving club flags, holding torches and chanting songs.

At his signing ceremony, Salah said: “The last couple of days, it’s an experience I’ve ⁠never had in my life. I just want to thank every one of you ​for being here today. I am ‌feeling so much love ‌here I never expected that reception.

“I ‌am here to win, I want to win something with this club because you showed me so much love – I appreciate that.”

Salah will receive a 20% share from products sold ‌under his name, plus conditional bonuses each season.

View image in fullscreen Mohamed Salah takes photos of the scenes in the stands after his first taste of life as one of Papara Park’s own. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

Salah left Liverpool after nine years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, winning the Premier League twice and the Champions League. His output waned last season and he was left ​on the bench in European games, leading to a public disagreement with Liverpool’s then manager Arne Slot.

Trabzonspor – generally considered to ​be the fourth-biggest team in Turkey after Fenerbahce, Galatasaray and ‌Besiktas – finished ​third in the ​Super Lig last season to qualify for the Europa League playoff round. They last won the league title in 2022.

Sports.title: Aston Villa transfer briefing: Players fear losing Ezri Konsa, the latest on Nicolas Jackson move and UEFA stumbling block, Matteo Ruggeri deal close and wingers on radar after Johan Manzambi injury blow
Sports.content:
Aston Villa transfer briefing: Players fear losing Ezri Konsa, the latest on Nicolas Jackson move and UEFA stumbling block, Matteo Ruggeri deal close and wingers on radar after Johan Manzambi injury blow

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Aston Villa supporters could be forgiven for feeling angry and confused. Barely two months after one of the greatest nights in their history, they have lost two of their most important players and more are expected to follow.

Under Unai Emery, the club have finished seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth in the Premier League. They have qualified for the Champions League twice, won the Europa League and will have a chance to add the UEFA Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain in Salzburg on Wednesday.

Yet because of UEFA’s maddening financial rules that appear designed to help revenue-generating monsters like Chelsea and Manchester United and punish ambitious rivals like Villa, Emery finds himself without Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers heading into the new season, after they joined United and Chelsea respectively for a combined £152million.

Left back Lucas Digne is expected to join PSG and centre back Ezri Konsa – another pillar of Emery’s best teams – is a target for Arsenal, with Liverpool also monitoring the situation.

There are positives, however. Pound for pound, Emery is perhaps the best coach in the league and he is still at Villa. Champions League football will boost the balance sheet and plans to take the capacity of Villa Park to 50,000 are moving ahead. That should also deliver improved revenue and a bigger transfer warchest.

Yet football is always about the here and now and Daily Mail Sport looks at where Villa stand...

Under Unai Emery, Aston Villa have qualified for the Champions League twice, won the Europa League and will have a chance to add the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg on Wednesday

It's been a tough transfer window for Villa fans, with Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans (pictured) leaving the club for a combined £152million

Could there be more outgoings?

FIRST SIX FIXTURES Weds PSG (n, Super Cup) Aug 23 Brighton (a, PL) Aug 31 Arsenal (h, PL) Sep 5 Hull (a, PL) Sep 12 N Forest (h, PL) Sep 19 Tottenham (a, PL)

The big one to watch after Digne is Konsa. At 28, the England defender is probably at the peak of his market value and heading into the summer he was one of three principal targets for Arsenal, along with Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior.

Guimaraes is due to sign for £75million this week and while Vinicius is set to stay at Real Madrid, Arsenal have not given up hope of landing Konsa, who is needed while they handle injuries to William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Ben White.

The champions will have to do better than the original offer, though, which was believed to be little more than half of Villa’s £60million valuation. That did not go down well with co-owner Nassef Sawiris, but it is thought the Villa squad are becoming increasingly resigned to Konsa’s departure.

There continues to be interest in Ollie Watkins, particularly from clubs in the Turkish top flight and the Saudi Pro League, though with so many experienced players already out of the door, it would be brave to let Watkins follow them. Though he turns 31 in December, Watkins has been Villa’s top scorer in every season since he joined the club in 2020, and is their leading all-time Premier League marksman.

It is a different matter with Tammy Abraham – another curious Villa transfer. Emery and his lieutenants pushed hard to sign Abraham for £18.2million from Besiktas in January yet it is thought that after only four starts Villa are prepared to let him go again, ideally on a permanent basis.

Earlier in the window, Villa were open to offers for Ross Barkley but with Tielemans leaving and Amadou Onana recovering from ACL damage, the former England man will not be placed on the market unless Villa can strengthen in midfield.

Arsenal are pushing to make Ezri Konsa (centre) the next big exit at Villa this summer

Tammy Abraham's £18.2million January move has not panned out and he could leave this summer

And what about incomings?

This is where it becomes tricky. Villa’s £54million club-record signing Johan Manzambi is not fit due to the knee injury he sustained playing for Switzerland at the World Cup.

Joao Gomes has made a promising start after joining for £38million from Wolves but more strength is needed in midfield, with Joao Palhinha still a target, though Bayern Munich would prefer to sell the Portugal international permanently.

Digne’s impending departure means another left back is needed, and Matteo Ruggeri could join from Atletico Madrid. The clubs have all but agreed terms on a deal worth about £15million for the Italian.

Alejandro Garnacho has joined on loan from Chelsea while Marseille winger Igor Paixao is another on Emery’s radar. Plenty of wingers have been observed this summer – from Ibrahim Mbaye to Harvey Barnes and Crysencio Summerville (who has since joined Al Hilal for £68million) – but Villa’s strong relationship with Chelsea helped get the Garnacho move over the line. Keep an eye on that for later in the window.

Then there is the striker. Ever since Emery joined the club, it feels like Villa have been looking for a forward to complement Watkins and ultimately succeed him. Jhon Duran had the talent to do so, but not the temperament. Donyell Malen did reasonably well when he played and his departure to Roma last January felt more of a financial move than a football one, given the constant pressure from UEFA rules. Quite simply, Abraham Part 2 simply has not worked.

Could Nicolas Jackson be the next one? At the moment, Villa are playing down interest in the Senegal forward. But Emery has always admired him since their days together at Villarreal and as highlighted, Villa and Chelsea have a good relationship.

But there's a hitch. UEFA rules state that permanent transfers between the same clubs within a 45-day period will be deemed ‘swaps’, which affects how profits can be recorded on balance sheets and stops any financial chicanery between teams.

The final day of the window is 41 days after Chelsea announced they had signed Rogers. Would that stop Villa signing Jackson? In such a frantic window, nothing can be ruled out – especially as players often sign for clubs some days before the official announcement.

Club-record signing Johan Manzambi is still recovering from the injury he suffered playing for Switzerland at the World Cup

Villa have all-but agreed a £15million deal with Atletico Madrid for Italian left back Matteo Ruggeri (left)

Emery's admiration for Nicolas Jackson dates back to their days together at Villarreal

How are Villa shaping up for the season?

Given the departure of Rogers, Villa need the Manzambi transfer to work and as things stand, the 20-year-old is unlikely to be fit for their Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23, and the early part of the season. Supporters are understandably alarmed at this summer's exodus while the squad are keen to see more high-level players join.

There is also a feeling, though, that Villa needed a refresh. The majority of last season’s squad had been at Villa throughout Emery’s four-year tenure and Villa knew they would have to sell this summer. Perhaps Emery would have preferred not to lose both Tielemans and Digne, who were key figures in the dressing room, but he will rarely stand in the way of a player who wishes to leave.

Roberto Olabe replaced Monchi as Villa’s transfer chief last September and this is his first summer window. Softly spoken and methodical, he is a much calmer figure than his predecessor and is a good counterbalance to the more instinctive Emery and director of football Damian Vidagany.

Villa started last season dreadfully, failing to score in any competition until September 16 and waiting until September 25 for their first win. It did not stop Emery’s men recording one of their best seasons in modern times, turning that first win into a run of 12 in 13 league matches as they roared back to finish fourth.

So a slow start is no reason to panic – but with so many changes to their team, Villa fans will struggle to stay calm if August goes awry.

Sports.title: FREDDIE BURNS interview: I beat the All Blacks on my England debut - then woke up at the training ground in a pile of my own sick
Sports.content:
Freddie Burns is laughing down the phone from Romania.

‘It was typical of me to miss out the slide on my Instagram post that actually said I was retiring,’ chuckles the former Bath, Gloucester, Leicester and England No 10.

‘I had to post it again separately just to make sure people were clear!’

In an 18-year professional rugby career, Burns, now 36, has always been an entertaining character. So, it was fitting he continued that trend when announcing it was coming to an end on social media this week.

In an era where most modern players trot out anodyne press conference quotes and seem reticent to show their true selves, Burns has always been an outlier.

‘I’ve had some good moments and some f****** low ones,’ says Burns, who will play one more season with Dinamo Bucharest before calling it quits.

Freddie Burns has announced he will retire from rugby later this year. 'I've had good moments and some f****** low ones,' he tells Daily Mail Sport

Burns kicked two penalties against the All Blacks on debut in 2012 as England stunned the world champions with a 38-21 hammering

He also became a Leicester cult hero, after kicking the drop-goal that sealed the Premiership title for the Tigers in 2012

He will depart as one of English club rugby’s cult heroes. A more-than-talented fly-half, whose last-gasp drop-goal sealed Leicester the PREM Rugby title in 2022, Burns won five England caps. His Test debut was one to remember. He kicked two penalties as a replacement in a famous 2012 victory over New Zealand. Not a bad way to start.

‘All I remember from that night was being hammered when I went up to collect my England cap at the post-match function at Twickenham,’ recalls Burns.

‘I was bumping into all these legends, guys like Richie McCaw and Dan Carter. I was s*** faced. It was just after the 2011 World Cup and all the shenanigans that had gone on there. Stuart Lancaster was the coach and the RFU were still trying to save some face. So, we drank hard at Twickenham, then got the bus back to Pennyhill Park instead of going out.

‘I woke up on the floor of the bathroom in my room at Pennyhill. It had a heated floor and there was a lovely little pile of sick cooking next to me. I was still wearing my suit.

‘I was quite glad we didn’t go out that night as there would probably have been a good chance I’d have ended up in the Thames!’

Burns adds: ‘As a boy, I lived down the road from where Bath trained. When I watched them, I remember thinking playing just a minute of PREM Rugby would have been enough for me. My career went miles beyond what I expected.

‘I could have played more for England. But I want to be grateful for the five caps I got, not the ones I didn’t. It was five more than most people get. I want to avoid being bitter about things that didn’t happen because I’ve had so many good ones that did. I want to be thankful for that.’

Burns played hard and celebrated harder. But his outgoing character – sadly all too rare in the game these days – shouldn’t distract from his on-field ability.

Three of Burns' five Tests came against New Zealand, scoring 20 points in two matches on England's 2014 tour

‘I could have played more for England. But I want to be grateful for the five caps I got, not the ones I didn’t'

Burns started at Gloucester, had two stints at Leicester, and also represented his home city of Bath. Rugby also gave him the chance to travel the world. He made trips to Japan and New Zealand with Shoki Shuttles and the Highlanders respectively and will end his playing days in one of the game’s more unusual outposts in Romania.

‘In rugby, there are a lot of very, very tough days with a few brilliant ones sprinkled in,' Burns says, 'One thing I’d say to young players now is make sure you enjoy your wins.

'That doesn’t mean you have to have 20 beers. Now, players focus on having their protein shake and a good sleep. When you have a good win, sit in the changing room with your mates you’ve gone to battle with. Enjoy having a drink or two. Share time with the opposition. It all goes by so quick.

'I definitely made the most of my career in terms of celebrating! But even now, I still wish I’d enjoyed certain moments more.

'One of my frustrations with rugby is that there are so many brilliant personalities in the game, but some lads don’t want to express themselves or say their opinion. The Six Nations Netflix documentary was so f****** boring. It didn’t show the personalities of the players. You’re starting to see that more now with guys like Henry Pollock. Hopefully it continues.’

If downing the All Blacks and slotting a PREM-winning drop-goal were Burns’ highs, one of the lows came in 2018. In action for Bath against Toulouse, he celebrated what should have been a try too early and Frenchman Maxime Medard knocked the ball from his grasp.

Burns broke through as a 19-year-old, having joined Gloucester from Bath's academy and going on to spend six seasons at Kingsholm

Burns celebrates too early while playing for Bath against Toulouse in a Champions Cup match and has the ball knocked out of his hand by Maxime Medard

‘The thing I’m most proud of in my career is my resilience,’ Burns says. ‘That’s what that incident taught me.

'The biggest frustration with that game is if I’d scored and we’d won, I reckon I’d have been man of the match! I had a brilliant game at full-back. I scored one and kicked a couple of long-range penalties. Yes, I s*** the bed at the end but on the whole, I was all right! I’m glad it happened because of the way my career panned out after that.

‘I went to Wasps the weekend after and I kicked well in a draw. I got off the bus there and immediately, there was a camera in my face. I knew it was what all the pundits were talking about. The keyboard warriors were after me.’

Burns celebrated winning the PREM in 2022 by doing the post-match press conference in his pants, before a big night out, a mammoth McDonald’s order and heading to bed with the trophy.

‘We partied hard. It was just a big feeling of relief,’ he says. ‘Before I’d come back to Leicester, I’d had to deal with the blow to the ego of going to Japan. It was one of the best things that happened to me, but at the time going to the Japanese second division at 30 was tough.

‘I was thinking, “F****** hell, is this where my career has gone?”.

‘The funniest stories have come from the hard times. When Aaron Mauger was coach at Leicester, he came in one day and put a Tigers shirt in the bottom of an empty bucket.

‘He gave each player an empty pint glass and said: “Go and fill your glass up with how much you’ve given to the shirt and what you’re willing to do for this club.”

‘Most guys filled their glasses two thirds or so full. One of the academy lads who hadn’t really played much walked up to the bucket so slowly because his cup was so full. We absolutely f****** hammered him for that!

'I don't really care what people thought of me as a player,' reflects Burns. 'But I'd always like to think they'd say I was a good bloke'

'I tried to never lose the love of the game. Sometimes I was s*** and sometimes I was OK, but I’d like to think the fans always saw I tried.

'I don’t really care what people thought of me as a player. People will think I’m good, bad and indifferent. But I’d always like to think that when my name comes out of someone’s mouth, they’d say I was a good bloke.

'If that’s all I’m remembered for, then I’ll be happy.’

Sports.title: Mexico turns on USA and Canada by BACKING Gianni Infantino as defiant FIFA chief refuses to quit over World Cup scheme
Sports.content:
The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) has caused shockwaves by choosing to back embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino and go directly against the USA, Canada and other Concacaf members.

Concacaf - the body that governs the sport in North America, Central America, and the Caribbean - joined the global revolt against Infantino last week and issued a damning statement against him.

Infantino has faced a major backlash since his plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup emerged last month. Amid widespread outrage and opposition, those plans were dumped.

But, on Thursday night, the FMF chose to go against Concacaf's position and released a statement throwing its weight behind Infantino.

It read: 'The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defense lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it.

'Therefore, the FMF will not recognize or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by President Infantino on August 5, 2026, to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations.

Mexico has gone against Concacaf and backed embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino

UEFA repeated its loss of confidence in Infantino and reiterated its World Cup boycott threat

'The FMF supports President Infantino's leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening.'

Not long after Mexico released its statement, the Argentinian federation did the same and said it wanted to 'express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years'.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has also reaffirmed its support for the president in recent days.

But Mexico's position comes in contrast to what Concacaf said in a statement published on social media on July 30. It read: 'Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release.

'We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process. We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

'As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport.

'Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship. This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the FIFA family will act in the same manner.'

But while Concacaf is clearly fractured, Daily Mail Sports understands UEFA is set to continue its boycott of the World Cup until Infantino is removed from his position.

Infantino is facing huge pressure over his failed plan to sell off stakes in the FIFA World Cup

European football’s governing body issued a statement on Thursday reiterating that it had lost confidence in the FIFA president in the wake of his aborted World Cup sell-off.

UEFA previously said that Infantino’s proposal would have to be withdrawn and that it would need assurances that such ‘attempts to disfigure the game this way will never be made again’ before it lifted its self-imposed ban.

However, it is believed that – as things stand - anything less than Infantino’s head would not be enough to ensure the likes of champions Spain, England, France and Germany take part in four years’ time.

An international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: ‘This had to be done. He has to go and this is the only way to force him out.’

On Wednesday night, FIFA announced Infantino had the backing of members of the body’s council after crisis talks in Morocco.

The beleaguered Swiss had summoned officials to his hotel as part of what appears to be, for now, a successful attempt to cling to power.

Following the hotel summit FIFA issued a statement saying execs had given their 'full support' to Infantino while acknowledging 'mistakes' in the dropped plan.

FIFA said they have now apologised in a letter to the various football associations and that a ‘review’ will be carried out.

Along with UEFA's continued anger, a withering statement from FIFPRO, the global union for professional footballers, hit out at Infantino and the FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme.

It read: 'FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) is gone. The abuse of power that produced it is not. Governance reforms, not a cover-up, are urgently needed.

The USA, Canada and other Concacaf members joined the backlash against Infantino

Donald Trump has denied any knowledge of Infantino's plan to sell off the World Cup

'The withdrawal of FFE was inevitable. But withdrawing the proposal does not erase what it revealed.

'A plan capable of permanently altering the ownership and governance of the FIFA World Cup, and commercialising the competitions built by generations of players, was conceived in secrecy, negotiated behind closed doors and brought to the brink of agreement before the FIFA Council, the Member Associations, players and football’s recognised stakeholders even knew it existed.

'That is not merely a governance failure. It is a profound abuse of presidential power.'

They also ripped into FIFA's latest update from its meeting in Morocco and called for 'structural safeguards to ensure these events can never be repeated'.

This includes legally binding engagement 'with professional football's stakeholders on decisions of major consequence' and voting rights for them on the FIFA council.

The statement concluded: 'The withdrawal of FFE prevented an irreversible decision. It did not restore the confidence that made such a proposal possible in the first place.

'That confidence has now been fundamentally broken. It cannot be rebuilt through carefully drafted statements, internal reviews or promises to improve processes. Nor can it be restored simply by announcing governance and structural reforms that should always have existed.

'These reforms are now indispensable. But they are the responsibility of the future, not an absolution of the past.

'The players did not create this crisis. They will insist that football emerges from it with stronger institutions, stronger safeguards and leadership worthy of the trust the game demands.'

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr signs new six-year deal at Real Madrid: Arsenal miss out on key transfer target after breakthrough in contract talks
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior has agreed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid, rejecting Arsenal’s keen attempt of luring the winger to north London.

The star has been offered improved terms in excess of £19million a year after stalling in contract negotiations, and that offer has been enough for him to commit his long-term future to the club.

Talks between the player's agents, general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place in Madrid on Wednesday. Jose Mourinho also underlined that the 26-year-old is also firmly in his plans.

Despite the increased confidence at the Bernabeu, the player added to the uncertainty on Wednesday night by deleting his entire Instagram history. Vinicius' page, which has 63.9million followers, currently displays no images or bio and he's also removed his profile picture.

But he has now committed his long-term future to the club, despite being open to a move to the Premier League champions if he could not agree terms.

The Gunners made initial enquiries into the player last week, with manager Mikel Arteta insisting that the Premier League winners will be 'very ambitious' during the summer's transfer window.

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr has signed a new six-year contract amid interest from Arsenal

But reports on Wednesday suggested Madrid were bullish about their chances of seeing off interest from north London – particularly with Mourinho's backing.

Vinicius posted on Instagram: ‘Eight years at the Bernabeu are too short... Six more years, and then forever.’

The club said in a statement: ‘Vinicius Jr has become one of the most important players in one of the most successful periods in our history.’

Arsenal would have accelerated their interest in the player if he had rejected Real's terms but the Premier League champions must now look elsewhere as they target an attacker.

It’s understood the Gunners have a few versatile forwards on their list which they had been monitoring during the Vinicius saga, for the possibility of him staying in Madrid.

One of the major sticking points in negotiations between Real and Vinicius' camp has been the re-signing fee. Talks have been ongoing for 18 months.

But the latest increase in their offer left Real confident that Vinicius Jr will commit his future to the Spanish giants.

Real did not want to lose the Brazilian on a free, with his contract set to expire in less than a year.

Mikel Arteta's side were hopeful of agreeing a deal if there was no breakthrough in contract talks between club and player

The player was thought to view any contract he signs with Los Blancos, where he has played since 2018, as the defining deal of his career – and recognition of his efforts for the club that in recent seasons have seen him become a Ballon d'Or contender in their colours.

Vinicius returned to join his team-mates at their pre-season camp on Monday to undergo the standard start-of-season medical tests and train for the first time under new manager Mourinho.

Arteta meanwhile has remained upbeat about his plans for the rest of the window, following the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

'We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously,' Arteta said following Arsenal's pre-season friendly against Girona.

'We want to get better like anybody else, and you can see the transfer market and our opponents... We won't sit still and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

'The margins are very small. Because we want to get better and the level is going to increase.

'We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team.'

Sports.title: Arsenal express interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero: Gunners ask star's agent about potential deal but Atletico Madrid strong favourites to land Spurs defender
Sports.content:
Arsenal express interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero: Gunners ask star's agent about potential deal but Atletico Madrid strong favourites to land Spurs defender

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Atletico Madrid remain favourites to sign Cristian Romero from Tottenham despite interest from fierce rivals Arsenal.

The Premier League champions are understood to have asked the agents of the Spurs captain what the deal would be.

Spurs are unaware of Arsenal’s interest and would be unwilling to consider selling 28-year-old Romero to their north London rivals.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last month, Atletico rekindled their interest as Inter Milan made their pitch.

Inter have agreed a £34m fee with Spurs but have not agreed on personal terms.

Atletico are working on exits before making their formal bid.

Cristian Romero is set to leave Tottenham and Arsenal asked what the deal would be

Atletico are in talks to sell left-back Matteo Ruggeri to Aston Villa in a deal worth £19.7m if the 24-year-old agrees to go and are also selling Nahuel Molina to Roma, with the combined fees to go towards a £30m bid for Romero.

The central defender is free to leave Spurs for the right price after the club bolstered their defensive ranks earlier in the transfer window.

The additions of Marcos Senesi on a free transfer and John Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52m mean Roberto de Zerbi is well stocked.

But the idea of selling the club captain to their arch rivals Arsenal would be deemed completely unacceptable by Spurs fans and the club would not countenance it.

Arsenal will be without William Saliba, who suffered a back injury at the World Cup, for months and are considering reinforcements at the back.

But Romero appears destined for a move away from the Premier League having spent the last five years at Tottenham after joining from Atalanta.

He was at the heart of Lionel Scaloni's defence for the Argentina side who beat England in the World Cup semi-final before suffering a 1-0 defeat by Spain in the final last month.

Romero has come close to leaving Spurs before, notably after Ange Postecoglou departed.

He suffered a knee injury during the club's dramatic run-in at the end of last season in which they fought off relegation.

Romero left the pitch in tears during a 1-0 defeat by Sunderland but De Zerbi managed to keep Spurs up without his captain, who recovered in time to play for Argentina.

He came under fire for celebrating in the faces of opposition players during the World Cup and also snubbed Donald Trump after the final defeat, ignoring the US President after collecting his runners-up medal.

After receiving his medal around his neck from Infantino, Romero snubbed Trump by not shaking his hand, instead he walked straight past him to join his team-mates.

Sports.title: Man City target new goalkeeper after James Trafford sale, Bruno Guimaraes nears £75m Arsenal move and Man United confirm signing of star, 18: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man City target new goalkeeper after James Trafford sale, Bruno Guimaraes nears £75m Arsenal move and Man United confirm signing of star, 18: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Arsenal interested in Spurs captain

Arsenal admire Cristian Romero - but a sale to the Gunners would not be contemplated by Tottenham.

The Spurs captain remains the subject of strong interest from Atletico Madrid and Inter who had a £34.2m fee in place.

Spurs meanwhile are preparing a new long-term contract for defender Micky van de Ven.

The Netherlands centre-back has a deal until 2029.

Spurs defender Ashley Phillips is joining Middlesbrough for £7m and the deal could rise to £20m with bonuses. Spurs have also negotiated a 20 per cent sell-on clause and matching rights into the transfer agreement.

Real get their Diomande

Real Madrid have reached an agreement with RB Leipzig to sign one-time Liverpool target Yan Diomande on a seven-year contract.

Real are paying a guaranteed fee of £107million for the 19-year-old, with the total deal worth up to £120m.

Yan Diomande - who was a target for Liverpool earlier this summer - has joined Real Madrid

Liverpool had an offer worth £85m rejected earlier in the window while PSG also tried to sign the Ivory Coast international. Diomande scored 13 goals and provided 10 assists in 36 appearances last season.

Liverpool are currently working to add PSG pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Nestory time at Sporting

Sporting Lisbon have agreed a deal worth around £17m for Watford forward Nestory Irankunda.

Bayern Munich have a 40 per cent sell-on clause for the Australia international and will be due around £7m.

Diomande in doubt

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest has hit a major snag with the deal now far from certain.

Forest had been close to agreeing a fee of about £35m with Sporting Lisbon for the centre-back but Daily Mail Sport understands talks have hit the buffers.

Oliver Glasner had made the centre-back his top target - as he did at Crystal Palace last summer, which also proved unsuccessful.

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest is understood to have hit a snag

It now remains to be seen if the transfer can be revived in the remaining days of the window.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Trafford completes Leeds switch

James Trafford has completed a move from Manchester City to Leeds in a deal that could reach £45m.

Trafford becomes the most expensive English goalkeeper of all time after the clubs struck an agreement on £40m plus £5m in add-ons.

Man City are closing on agreement with Marseille for goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli.

The 34-year-old will cost around £2.9million and will replace Trafford.

The deal will allow Lucas Perri to move from Leeds to Torino. The Italians are waiting for Perri to recover from a small injury which kept him out of Leeds' last two pre-season games before finalising the move.

Leeds have a list of around five goalkeepers as they plot their search for Trafford's deputy.

They have Alex Cairns but want another to cover Perri's departure too.

San Lorenzo's Paraguay international Orlando Gill is one but they are yet to make an offer.

Dykes snubs Charlton for Millwall

Scotland striker Lyndon Dykes has agreed a one-year deal with Millwall.

The 30-year-old has completed a medical and is finalising his move.

Dykes rejected a longer term offer from Charlton Athletic, where he spent the second half of last season, as he looks to help Millwall earn promotion.

Scotland forward Lyndon Dykes is set to join Millwall

Villa and Toon keep tabs on defender

Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas is attracting attention from Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

The 19-year-old can play left back and centre back and has also been watched by Barcelona and Manchester United scouts.

Some of the clubs view him as a player for the future while others are considering a bid this month.

Bruno heads to the capital

Bruno Guimaraes is understood to be in London to finalise his £75million move to Arsenal.

The 28-year-old left Newcastle's pre-season camp on Wednesday after a fee of £75m was agreed with Arsenal. Newcastle are continuing to work on a replacement.

Napoli have enquired about striker Gabriel Jesus at Arsenal.

Bruno Guimaraes is in London to complete his move from Newcastle to Arsenal

Gunners keep tabs on the next Kvaratskhelia

Arsenal scouts were at Larne's Europa League qualifier against Iberia 1999 on Tuesday.

They were understood to be running the rule over the Georgian side's attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili.

The exciting 17-year-old has been on Arsenal's radar for a number of months and has been compared in style to compatriot Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at Paris St Germain.

Indeed, the French side are also understood to be among his admirers as well as clubs in Italy.

Bartishvili is on loan at Iberia from Kolkheti 1913, however, he is expected to be sold in the coming days as interest intensifies.

Hammers confirm Veltman

West Ham have confirmed the signing of former Brighton defender Joel Veltman.

The Dutch defender has signed a one-year contract with an option for a second year.

'I'm delighted to have signed, and I can't wait to get started,' said Veltman. 'The project here really excites me.'

'I spoke to Nuno [Espírito Santo], as well as my family and my agent, and everything added up. We know that West Ham need to be in the Premier League, and for sure that is our goal for the season.

'I think I bring my experience, my winning mentality and togetherness. I bring leadership - I've been the captain at Ajax, and I enjoy talking to my teammates and using my experience to help the squad.

'I'm just so excited to give everything, to meet my new teammates and to see all the supporters too.'

West Ham are also prepared to break the Championship transfer record of £17.5m to sign Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar. Talks have opened between the clubs.

Talks for Spurs winger Manor Solomon are currently off over bonus payments.

Barcelona have finally expressed their interest in Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri

Rodri was keen on a move to Madrid but equally is understood to be open to joining Barca's project where eight of the national team are in the current squad.

The 21-year-old's former club Blackburn are due a sell on percentage.

A central defender became Boro's priority after Dael Fry's decision to leave for Birmingham at the end of his contract.

Spain winger Victor Munoz reported to Liverpool training for the first time yesterday following his £34.5million move from Osasuna.

Munoz was the first new addition after the arrival of head coach Andoni Iraola.

Sports.title: The task facing Mykhailo Mudryk after his 20-month ban: Rio Ferdinand hit the ground running for Man United, Paul Pogba's fitness woes and Diego Maradona's mixed spell in Spain after their lengthy suspensions
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk's long-awaited return to football came on Tuesday as Chelsea winger came on as a late substitute in their friendly against Juventus.

Mudryk's brief cameo – a 10-minute appearance – came after his doping ban came to an end this week after a resolution was reached with the Football Association.

The £89million signing had not played since November 2024, when he started and scored away at Heidenheim in the Conference League, after he had been suspended from football after failing a doping test for the banned substance meldonium.

Daily Mail Sport revealed this week that Chelsea have already been approached by clubs to ask about their plans for Mudryk this season.

Whatever outcome is reached, there is an understanding patience will be required with Mudryk having been out of the game for 20 months.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at previous examples of how other players have got on after returning to the game from long bans from football.

Mykhailo Mudryk made his return to football this week after his 20-month doping ban ended

Clubs are interested in a move for the Chelsea winger with an acceptance he will need time to return to his best after 20 months out of the game

Rio Ferdinand – Eight-month ban

The task facing Mudryk is outlined by Ferdinand's comments after returning from his doping ban in September 2004.

'Physically and mentally is was all new again, eight months out is a long time,' Ferdinand said after making his return.

Ferdinand had been hit with an eight-month ban from football and a £50,000 fine back in 2003. He had been sanctioned after failing to provide a drugs sample following a training session on September 23 that year.

His ban officially began in January 2004, starting days after he had been forced off injured during Man United's 1-0 defeat by Wolves.

Ferdinand, who failed in an appeal against his ban in March, was forced to watch from the sidelines as Man United suffered a dip in form in his absence and ultimately missed out on retaining their Premier League title. The ban also forced him to miss Euro 2004.

He ultimately made his return in September, with Sir Alex Ferguson throwing Ferdinand straight into the starting line-up as Man United hosted rivals Liverpool at Old Trafford.

Ferdinand required an energy bar to help him through the match, having not been able to play in friendlies to get him back up to speed.

Rio Ferdinand returned from an eight-month ban in September 2004 for Manchester United

Ferdinand played the full 90 minutes on his return as Man United earned a 2-1 win over Liverpool

Sir Alex Ferguson hailed Ferdinand's performance as 'superb' in their victory

Ferguson hailed his performance as 'superb' and highlighted how Ferdinand's composure had helped his side, as Man United earned a 2-1 win courtesy of two Mikel Silvestre goals.

'The fans were fantastic as soon as I came out for the warm-up and even after they were brilliant,' Ferdinand told Sky Sports post-match.

'It is just nice to get out there and play, you forget about everything that has gone on beforehand but once you get out there and start warming up and game starts, it is all about football.

'It was never going to be easy, I was under no illusions that I was going to have an easy game. It was nervous energy, I needed some sugar intake and the physio brought around a little bar to chew on. It was obvious needed, eight months is a long time.

'I am not looking back, I am looking forward and continue playing football now and do what I love doing.'

Having made a stuttering start to the season by winning of their opening five matches, Man United's form picked up after Ferdinand's return to action with the defender also immediately earning a recall to the England squad.

Ferdinand was close to being an ever-present for Man United after his return to action, missing just two league matches in the remainder of the campaign.

Eric Cantona – Eight-month ban

One of the most famous bans in football history was handed to Cantona after he kung-fu kicked a Crystal Palace supporter in January 1995.

The Frenchman had launched himself into the crowd having reacted to goading from one supporter, following his red card in the match.

Man United initially suspended Cantona until the end of the season, but the Football Association ultimately extended his ban for eight months.

Cantona returned in stunning fashion on October 1 as Man United faced Liverpool, with home fans at Old Trafford turning up to the clash with French flags adorning his face to mark his comeback.

Eric Cantona was famously banned for eight months after kung-fu kicking a Crystal Palace fan

Cantona scored and assisted in his return as Man United drew 2-2 with Liverpool in 1995

The Man United talisman made an instant impact by setting up Nicky Butt for the opening goal. With Man United having then fallen behind, Cantona then scored from the penalty spot to secure a 2-2 draw.

'It's Eric's stage, Eric's the lead actor and Eric delivers the best lines,' Man United forward Brian McClair reflected to Sky Sports.

'It was as if he'd never been away,' added Steve Bruce. 'It was quite incredible that somebody who had been away for so long could come back and have the impact he did straight away, and it lifted everybody.'

Cantona proved the inspiration for Man United to complete a league and FA Cup double. The Frenchman top scored with 19 goals in all competitions including netting against Liverpool in the FA Cup final, a match where he captained the Red Devils.

He was named as the Football Writers Association's Player of the Season.

Adrian Mutu – Seven-month ban

Mutu was part of the Roman Abramovich led revolution at Chelsea in 2003, with the Romanian among ten players the Blues splashed out on that summer.

The £15.8million signing scored ten goals in 36 matches during his debut season at the club after joining from Parma.

Mutu would ultimately fall out with his new manager Jose Mourinho at the start of the following season amid concerns over his lifestyle. Mutu then tested positive for cocaine use in September 2004 and was handed a seven-month ban from football.

Chelsea sacked the forward as a result with the Blues chasing £15.2million in compensation.

'Taking cocaine during my time at Chelsea was the worst decision I could have made in my career,' Mutu reflected in an interview last year.

'I was alone and sad, but neither depression nor anything else justified my actions. Zero tolerance – that was Chelsea's policy regarding drugs. And I think that's fair.

Adrian Mutu had been one of Chelsea's high-profile signings of the early Roman Abramovich era

Mutu was sacked by Chelsea after a positive test for cocaine, and the club then demanded he paid £15.2m in compensation

The Romanian forward spent a season at Juventus, before rebuilding his career at Fiorentina

'I made a mistake, strayed from the path, and paid the price for it. I was caught off guard. I wasn't used to that life. I was unprepared.

'I arrived at Chelsea during a turbulent time in my personal life, and I found myself caught up in too many excuses and lies. I was too young and too alone.

'I've reflected on that many times. I believe that for more than a season, I was amongst the best players in the world, so I could have won it easily. But bad decisions prevented me from doing so. I try not to beat myself up about it.'

Mutu was handed an almost immediate chance to return to the game with Juventus signing him in January 2005, despite his suspension running until May.

He scored seven goals in 32 league matches the following season as the Old Lady won Serie A – before later being stripped of their title.

Mutu moved on to Fiorentina in the summer of 2006 and spent five seasons at the club, scoring 54 goals in 112 league appearances. This led to Mutu being inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2024.

The forward had served a nine-month ban in 2010 after a failed doping test.

Paul Pogba – 18-month ban

Pogba's case represents an interesting comparison to Mudryk's owing to the similar length of time out of the game.

The French midfielder, like Mudryk, was initially facing a four-year ban from football with Pogba having tested positive for the prohibited substance DHEA in September 2023, when he was playing for Juventus.

His suspension was later reduced to 18 months following an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Pogba told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

The former Man United star was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance.

The World Cup winner, however, had already endured a series of injuries during his second spell at Juventus and Pogba's time on the sidelines during his ban also left him playing catch up.

Monaco had given Pogba his own fitness plan and planned to gradually introduce him into the team following his long absence.

Paul Pogba signed for Monaco last summer and viewed the move as a second chance after his 18 month doping ban ended

Pogba, however, spent much of the season on the sidelines amid a series of fitness issues

The 33-year-old managed just 115 minutes last season with Monaco considering his future

The 33-year-old ultimately played just 115 minutes for the Ligue 1 side last season as he struggled for fitness and form, with Monaco considering whether to part ways with him this summer.

Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro said last month: 'It is a complicated topic because we have a lot of respect for Paul, for the person he is. Since he arrived, he has been very positive.

'It is also true that, last year, the project didn't work well because when we started with him in the summer, the expectations were very different to what happened. I think that we have to be fair with him, follow his preparation every week, how he will progress physically and technically and then it will be the manager's decision.

'We have the summer to see what level we will see from Pogba. He could [leave at the end of the summer]. With Paul, it has always been a very open and transparent relationship.

'If, at some point, the expectations of the player are different to the expectations of the club, we will have to speak to find a solution. The performance will give all the answers that we need. Maybe he will stay, maybe he will leave.'

Diego Maradona – 15-month ban

The legendary Argentine was banned from football for 15 months back in 1991 after testing positive for cocaine.

The sanction effectively ended his historic spell at Napoli, who he had inspired to win two league titles, the Copa Italia and UEFA Cup.

Maradona looked to rebuild his career at Sevilla after his ban came to an end, as he joined forces with Carlos Bilardo, who had been Argentine's coach for their 1986 World Cup triumph.

His arrival proved lucrative for Sevilla with the club holding marquee friendlies during pre-season, with the club said to have enjoyed a £2.5million uptick in revenues during his sole year at the club.

Diego Maradona spent a season at Sevilla after serving a 15-month suspension from football

Maradona was initially seen as having a positive impact at the club, despite being overweight after the prolonged spell out of the game. Maradona, who was given the captain's armband after signing, helped the club into the top three of the LaLiga table early on.

The 32-year-old also produced an inspired performance in a 2-0 victory over Real Madrid.

His off-the-field problems, however, derailed Maradona during the second half of the season, leading to Sevilla hiring a detective to track him.

A falling out with Bilardo also contributed to Maradona spending just a single season at Sevilla, who finished seventh in the league, before he returned to Argentina.

Sports.title: Alleged scammer who 'targeted NFL players in million-dollar scheme' found dead in swimming pool at 24
Sports.content:
The alleged mastermind of a million-dollar scam targeting sports stars has reportedly been found dead in a swimming pool.

An investigation has been launched into the death of Mohamed Coulibaly, 24, after his body was discovered at a house in Harrison Township, New Jersey.

According to ABC, police officers visited the home after family members expressed concerns about Coulibaly.

Only last month, the 24-year-old from Philadelphia was named by Barron's as the organizer of an alleged scam that attempted to lure ex-NFL players and other athletes into buying a stake in 'bogus websites.'

According to Barron's, Coulibaly allegedly hoped to dupe the athletes into believing they were investing in successful businesses. Instead, three ex-NFL players claimed to have lost more than $1million combined.

Among those who allegedly fell victim to the scam was former New York Giants linebacker Tae Crowder. He reportedly invested his life savings - worth $500,000 - into one of Coulibaly's ventures.

The alleged mastermind of a scam targeting sports stars has reportedly been found dead in a swimming pool

Among those who allegedly fell victim to the scam was ex-New York Giants star Tae Crowder

'We were just, every day, talking about different investments and different things we could possibly get into. I saw him hanging out with a bunch of different guys that I know, which you know made me feel comfortable,' Crowder recalled, per ABC.

'I would log into the store all the time and just see how it would work and what was going on. I feel like the more I told him about that, as many times I kept logging in, the number started going up.'

But Crowder claims he never saw any return on his investment. 'I don't want anybody else to get involved in anything like this, and whoever has got involved, I just want to come together and make it right.'

According to Barron's, Coulibaly claimed investors had not received any money because he was still waiting for funds himself.

At the time of his death, ABC reports, no criminal charges had been filed related to the alleged scheme.

A GoFundMe page, purportedly created by Mohamed's brother, Badra, has raised nearly $13,000. The family is 'urgently working to bring him home so he can be laid to rest with dignity and peace.' Coulibaly previously told Barron's that he immigrated to the US as a child with his Malian family.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford clause emerges as Barcelona transfer swoop causes issues
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford clause emerges as Barcelona transfer swoop causes issues

There's still plenty of business to be done in the transfer window at Manchester United with further high-profile arrivals and exits on the cards

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is on his first pre-season tour as Manchester United boss (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have been reasonably busy in the transfer market - but there could still be plenty more to come before the deadline. With Michael Carrick preparing for his first full season in charge, his side remain active on several high-profile fronts.

‌



Their midfield has already been strengthened by the arrivals of Andrey Santos from Chelsea in a £50million deal and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa for £35m. Even so, United are still believed to be in the market for at least one more man in the centre of the park.

‌



Attention will also soon turn to trimming the squad. Most notably, there's the question of what to do with Marcus Rashford, who is currently in limbo after being denied a move to Barcelona.

‌



With less than a month remaining before the transfer window closes and negotiations gathering pace across Europe, Mirror Football takes a look at the latest Manchester United transfer headlines.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist READ MORE :

Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical READ MORE :

Rashford contract clause emerges

United's efforts to move Rashford on this summer have been handed an added sense of urgency after details of a lucrative clause in his contract came to light. The 28-year-old currently earns an estimated £300,000 a week at Old Trafford, but that figure is now set to rise after United secured a return to the Champions League.

‌



View 3 Images Rashford is set for a seven-figure bonus on top of his hefty United wages if he stays put (Image: Getty)

Before Sir Jim Ratcliffe overhauled the club's wage structure, United players were entitled to an automatic 25 per cent pay rise if the club qualified for Europe's premier competition. That bonus scheme was scrapped in 2024, but existing contracts signed beforehand - including those of Rashford and Mason Mount - still contain the clause.

With Rashford already earning roughly £16m a year, his salary is expected to increase by around £4m following United's Champions League qualification. It only strengthens the club's desire to find a buyer before the transfer window closes.

‌



For much of the summer, a permanent move to Barcelona appeared the most likely outcome after his loan spell in Catalonia. However, the Spanish champions' £70m signing of Anthony Gordon looks to have ended that possibility. With just over three weeks remaining in the window, both player and club are running out of time to resolve his future.

Barcelona swoop causes problem for Man Utd

Barcelona's surprise move for Manchester City midfielder Rodri could have a significant knock-on effect on United's transfer plans. Real Madrid had appeared to be leading the race for the Spain captain, whose contract at the Etihad Stadium has less than a year left. Jose Mourinho's side were reportedly willing to pay upwards of £60m for the 30-year-old and City are open to cashing in.

View 3 Images Rodri is being chased by Spain's two biggest clubs (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

For United, a move to the Bernabeu would be the ideal outcome. Rodri's arrival could pave the way for Aurelien Tchouameni to leave, since the club would need to free up space in midfield and raise funds to keep their finances in check. The France international remains high on United's wishlist.

But convincing Real Madrid to part with him looks highly is they lose out on a midfielder of Rodri's calibre. Barcelona's interest has now complicated the equation. Should the Catalan giants win the race for Rodri, Real Madrid would have little reason to entertain offers for Tchouameni - dealing a major blow to United's hopes of pulling off a late midfield coup.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr agreement, Ezri Konsa twist, new Declan Rice issue
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr agreement, Ezri Konsa twist, new Declan Rice issue

Arsenal are continuing their hard work in the summer transfer window after missing out on numerous targets

View 4 Images Vinicius Junior has made his decision (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Arsenal are shifting their focus to other transfer targets as Real Madrid close in on a new deal for Vinicius Jr. Mikel Arteta was keen to bring the Brazilian winger to the Emirates Stadium but it is increasingly likely that he will remain in Spain.

‌



The Gunners are close to completing a transfer of their own with a £75million bid accepted for Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes. The midfielder has reportedly completed his medical and will sign a four-year deal in north London.

‌



Christos Tzolis, Illan Meslier and Piero Hincapie have already joined Arsenal for a combined £68.5m. Riccardo Calafiori has insisted his team must continue to add high-quality stars to their ranks as he targets more silverware.

‌



Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed READ MORE :

The defender told Sky Sports: "Of course we are on that level now, we are on top. We want to win the league again and we want to be even better than last season, if we can, so we need those kind of players, I think."

Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the red side of north London.

‌



Vinicius Jr agreement

View 4 Images Vini Jr is looking increasingly likely to remain in Spain (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Reports claim that Real are close to agreeing an extension for Vini Jr, putting any plans of Arteta securing the winger to bed. Fabrizio Romano states that the verbal agreement is nearly finalised, with the 26-year-old giving "the green light" to move forward with a new long-term deal.

Real manager Jose Mourinho has reportedly pushed for Vini to stay, stating that he was ready to welcome the winger back into the fold. Speaking ahead of the Brazilian's return to pre-season training, Mourinho said: "I’m concerned about not having everyone, and I would like to have three weeks of work with the others. It’s not possible.

‌



"On Monday, Vini Jr, Brahim, and Bernardo will arrive. Little by little, until the boys who played in the World Cup semifinals and final arrive, with the final being only Cucurella."

Ezri Konsa twist

View 4 Images Ezri Konsa has a few Premier League sides to choose from (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool are threatening to rival Arsenal for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa thanks to their major defensive crisis. Joe Gomez was injured during pre-season with Jeremy Jacquet yet to feature and Virgil van Dijk still on a break after the World Cup.

‌



The Gunners registered an interest in Konsa following William Saliba's back injury at the World Cup, but Villa's £60m price tag is thought to be above what they are willing to pay. The 28-year-old is a Premier League veteran and with two years left on his deal, he could be a great addition to either Liverpool or Arsenal.

Discussing the Reds' depth issues in defence, Andoni Iraola said: "With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes."

‌



Declan Rice issue

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes and Declan Rice both operate in the same area (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Guimaraes' imminent arrival at Arsenal could spell trouble for Declan Rice. The England international could be forced into an unnatural position in the squad.

Rice has been Arsenal's ever-reliable No. 8, making 158 appearances as the club's main playmaker. However, Guimaraes also operates in the creative slot and could shift the 27-year-old to a deeper No. 6 area.

‌



While this may create an issue for the duo, Jay Bothroyd believes they are "up there" with the best midfield pairing in the Premier League.

He said: "I do believe with Rice and Guimaraes, of all of those [Rodri and Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo, Matheus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali], I would probably say, as athletes as well as football players, they would be the best partnership in terms of fitness, physicality, both boxes.

"I think tactically, Rodri and Elliot Anderson might be better, but I think definitely for the way Arsenal play, I wouldn't swap that pairing for any of the others."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino offered shock lifeline as under-fire FIFA chief's World Cup final plan pays off
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino offered shock lifeline as under-fire FIFA chief's World Cup final plan pays off

Gianni Infantino has been under severe scrutiny as of recent due to his controversial plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors, with calls for his resignation flooding in

View 2 Images CAF have backed Gianni Infantino (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

The Confederation of African Football executive committee has "unanimously reconfirmed" support in Gianni Infantino, after widespread calls for the FIFA president to lose his job. The 56-year-old executive sparked outrage last week with proposals to sell a stake of the World Cup to private investors.

‌



The move, which was dubbed the 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' was swiftly met with widespread criticism, with UEFA vowing to boycott the tournament outright should plans have proceeded. The backlash ultimately prompted Infantino to shelve his proposals, which he dubbed to be an act of consolation rather than concrete plans that World Football were planning on rolling out.

‌



However, that hasn't prevented the Italian from seeing calls for his axing in the days since, with furious football fans and governing bodies outraged by the notion. Having held an emergency meeting in Rabat, executives instilled their faith in Infantino, sharing a scathing public statement which hit out at "attacks on its integrity."

‌



It read: "As previously communicated, the FFE proposal, which would have been subject to the approval of the FIFA Member Associations and the FIFA Council, is now off the table.

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

"With the project withdrawn, it was agreed that FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.

"There are always lessons to be learned, and FIFA will continue to improve its processes in light of this experience. In this instance, however, it is important to stress that, although mistakes were made, everything that was done was done in full compliance with the FIFA regulatory framework."

‌



And now, CAF have reaffirmed their commitment to Infantino with a statement of their own, in a major boost to the likelihood of the head of World Football retaining his job. It read: "The CAF EXCO also unanimously reconfirmed its support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino and thanked him for his support for African Football, over the years.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's relationship with Donald Trump also raised eyebrows after a phone call over a red card (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"President Infantino, the FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström and the FIFA Administration were also thanked for organizing a very successful FIFA World Cup 2026."

The President of CAF, Dr Patrice Motsepe, also said: "CAF welcomes and endorses the 'Joint Update' by FIFA President Gianni Infantino and Secretary General Mattias Grafström. CAF will continue to focus on making African Football amongst the best in the world and is reaffirming its commitment to adhering to global governance, transparency and auditing best practices.

"For us in Africa, adherence to governance, due process and transparency is crucial and non-negotiable, as this is the practice and conduct we expect from our governments, business and other institutions and organisations. This is also the conduct that is expected from CAF.

‌



We are committed to continue working together with FIFA, its Member Associations, other Football Confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of Football worldwide.

Good progress is being made in discussions with our current and new sponsors, partners and investors to ensure that CAF continues to be financially self-supporting and independent and that stadiums and other Football infrastructure is constructed and upgraded.

It comes as Africa have remained one of Infantino's biggest supporters since his election a decade ago, with the 2030 World Cup set to be held across Morocco, Portugal and Spain. Infantino has also offered Morocco the chance to host the final of the tournament at their brand-new 115,000-seat Hassan II stadium in Casablanca.

Sports.title: Man Utd finally announce sixth summer transfer as statement confirms next steps
Sports.content:
Man Utd finally announce sixth summer transfer as statement confirms next steps

Manchester United have been working to add to their squad at both senior and youth level in the transfer window and have confirmed the official capture of another player

View Image Cristian Orozco is now officially a Manchester United player (Image: Zohaib Alam/Manchester United FC)

Manchester United have confirmed that Cristian Orozco has officially joined them as their sixth capture of the transfer window.

‌



The 18-year-old attacking midfielder joins the Red Devils from Fortaleza CEIF, who play in the Colombian Categoria Primera A. Orozco is a Colomba Under-18 international and highly-rated for the future.

‌



Orozco's move was made official last month when he turned 18, though United did not immediately confirm the transfer. The statement announcing his move to England, shared on Thursday night, confirmed the talented teenager will initially link up with United's academy.

‌



Reports outlining the agreement struck by United to bring Orozco to Old Trafford emerged last year, with the youngster later confirming he visited Carrington back in December.

Man Utd forced to fork out millions as Marcus Rashford benefits from contract loophole READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist READ MORE :

Speaking to ESPN Colombia about the move, he said: "I know my strengths are my physicality and my technique.

"I have those qualities and, with the gift God gave me, I don’t think it will be too difficult. But everything is about adapting. I’m very young and that’s what I’ll need to do."

‌



He added: "I expect to learn a lot of English. When I was there, I realised just how, how important it is.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"I want to arrive and learn as quickly as possible. That’s what’s required so I can show my level and everything I’m capable of. I want to adapt to everything that comes my way as quickly as possible."

‌



While Orozco is set to link up with the academy, United have strengthened in midfield at a more senior level.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been signed from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively as part of United's plans to overhaul their engine room with the possibility that a further midfielder will be signed before the transfer deadline.
