World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: BJP MLAs storm well, disrupt Jharkhand assembly over exam irregularities
World.content:
Opposition BJP MLAs disrupted proceedings of the Jharkhand Assembly over alleged irregularities in a job examination, with several legislators entering the well of the House in protest.

Proceedings of the Jharkhand Assembly were adjourned till 12.30 pm amid an uproar by the BJP MLAs.

During the proceedings, BJP leader Babulal Marandi demanded a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities under a court-monitored panel.

Opposition MLAs raised placards and shouted slogans, including "stop selling students' future" and "recommend a CBI probe into irregularities in JPSC examination", targeting the JMM-led government.

BJP chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleged that the CID probe into the suspected job exam scam had been initiated to "cover up the issues".

"It is an eyewash. The youth doesn't have faith in the CID probe. The protesters will get justice only when a CBI team probes into the irregularities raised by the protesters," Jaiswal said, as cited by PTI.

The protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Friday, with six demonstrators continuing their hunger strike.





Meanwhile, two student unions announced plans to march to the state Assembly, which is currently in session, during the day.

The demonstrators have been demanding the cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination and an independent probe into the alleged irregularities in the recruitment test, either by the CBI or by a panel of retired High Court judges from outside the state.

World.title: India, China agree to use diplomatic, military channels to avoid LAC misunderstandings: MEA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and China have agreed to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels to address outstanding issues and prevent misunderstandings along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Thursday.

World.title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
World.content:
Aule On-screen setup running multibody dynamics simulations and tracking system capturing hardware test data for position and velocity for correlation

Aule 2: Dark room hardware test setup where the team recreated on-orbit lighting conditions with a sun simulator and a target mounted on a robotic arm to simulate the targetâs motion.

BENGALURU: What if satellites could simply plug into a power bank instead of drifting away when they run out of fuel? Thatâs the idea driving a Bengaluru startup building âjetpackâ satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft, take over their propulsion duties and keep billion-dollar assets working years longer.After recently validating a key part of its technology at an Isro facility used for Indiaâs SpaDeX docking mission, Aule Space is now preparing for what could become one of the worldâs most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations.For satellite operators, running out of fuel doesnât necessarily mean spacecraft have reached the end of life. In many cases, expensive communication satellites remain fully functional, but can no longer maintain their assigned orbital positions because they have exhausted the propellant needed for station-keeping. Once that happens, operators are forced to retire assets worth hundreds of millions of dollars.Aule has found another way. âWeâre trying to build satellites which can go and dock to existing satellites in space which donât have any installed ports... and extend their life so that they can keep generating revenue,â CEO Jay Panchal, told TOI. âItâs like a power bank,â he added.Instead of attempting the far more complicated task of refuelling satellites in orbit, Auleâs approach is to send a smaller âjetpackâ spacecraft that docks with an existing communications satellite and assumes responsibility for station-keeping using its own propulsion system.The company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build and generate significant annual revenues.The challenge lies in docking with satellites that were never designed to be serviced. Rather than relying on dedicated docking ports, Aule will attach its spacecraft to the liquid apogee motor (LAM) nozzle, a standard external feature found on most geostationary satellites.If successful, the technology could help operators extract years of additional service from satellites that would otherwise become orbital relics. Panchal said each docked âjetpackâ could extend a satelliteâs operational life by up to 5 years.*Key Test Done*The startup recently completed a major milestone by testing its camera-based guidance, navigation and control system at the Rendezvous Simulation Laboratory (RSL) at Isroâs ISITE â the same lab where critical elements of the SpaDeX were validated.âWe were the first non-govt entity to access RSL. This is the best kind of on-ground testing we can do for these capabilities,â Panchal said.One of Auleâs differentiators is its reliance on computer vision instead of multiple specialised sensors. Current docking systems typically use LiDAR, infrared cameras and other sensors. Aule says its spacecraft will perform the critical final approach using a single optical camera powered by onboard AI.The visual navigation models are trained using data generated in its own facilities and validated at Isroâs testbed before being deployed in orbit.The company is targeting an in-orbit demonstration next year, when it plans to launch two satellites that will autonomously dock in low-Earth orbit. Panchal claims it could be the worldâs first private mission to perform non-cooperative docking in LEO using camera-only navigation. The mission will validate technologies that Aule ultimately intends to deploy around geostationary communication satellites.

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhandâs largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee."Congress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms."We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site."He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.

NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. "These have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action," the reply said.In its response, the ministry said the rehabilitation plan for Scheduled Tribe families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project was based on a proposal submitted by the National Water Development Agency in 2016.Citing the 2016 proposal, the ministry said the project's first phase is expected to displace 1,913 families comprising 8,339 people, including 648 Scheduled Tribe families.Responding to questions on gram sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), the ministry said it does not maintain centralised records of meeting dates, attendance, signatures, grievances related to consent, compensation and displacement, or the status of their disposal, as implementation of the law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments and Union Territory administrations.The ministry added that it has repeatedly urged states and UTs to ensure that no eligible beneficiary is denied forest rights and to strictly comply with Section 4(5) of the FRA, which prohibits the eviction or removal of claimants from forest land under their occupation until the process of recognition and verification of their rights has been completed.The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district over issues related to displacement, rehabilitation and resettlement.As part of the agitation, protesters staged a series of symbolic demonstrations in July, including a "jal satyagraha", "chita (pyre) satyagraha" and "faansi satyagraha".The protest also included an indefinite hunger strike by activist Amit Bhatnagar, who was later forcibly removed from the site by state police. Nearly 150 villagers were also removed during the operation, visuals of which drew nationwide attention.

NEW DELHI: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles are on the verge of overtaking petrol-powered models in India, with CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 40.6% of passenger vehicle retail sales in July, just behind petrolâs 41.7%, according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) Thursday. The gap has narrowed sharply from 13.2 percentage points a year ago to just over a percentage point, reflecting a rapid shift in buyer preferences.The trend came as Indiaâs automobile retail market recorded its strongest-ever July performance, with overall registrations rising 25.8% year-on-year to a record 25.9 lakh units. For the first time, all six vehicle categories â two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, tractors and wheeled construction equipment â posted their highest-ever July retail volumes, underscoring broad-based demand across the industry.Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July. Within the segment, CNG vehicles accounted for 24.6% of sales, hybrids for 8% and electric vehicles for 7.9%. While hybrid vehicles continue to use petrol as their primary fuel source, automakers classify them as alternative-fuel vehicles because they combine an internal combustion engine with an electric powertrain to improve efficiency and reduce emissions.Petrolâs share, meanwhile, declined to 41.6% from 47.6% a year earlier. FADA said fresh model launches, affordability gains following GST changes and consumersâ increasing focus on lower running costs supported demand for alternative powertrains. The dealersâ body also noted that uncertainty surrounding the transition to E20 fuel appears to have nudged some buyers towards CNG, hybrid and EVs.The transition was equally evident in the two-wheeler market. Electric two-wheelers accounted for a record 11.2% of retail sales in July, up from 7.7% a year earlier.Overall EV retail registrations across all vehicle segments climbed to an all-time high of 3.28 lakh units during the month, taking EV penetration to about 12.7% of total vehicle retail sales from 9.6% a year ago. Maruti Suzuki retained its lead in the PV market in July, retailing over 1.6 lakh units.

World.title: Survey: 81% of study-abroad aspirants plan to return home
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The foreign degree may be global, but the career plan is largely homeward-bound: 81% of Indian study-abroad aspirants surveyed by Oxford International said they planned to return to India after completing their courses.

Nearly nine in 10 were the first in their family to pursue education overseas, while almost half said the decision to go abroad was their own.

The findings are part of the third edition of Student Global Mobility Index, which combines 17,925 responses to core questions with about 2,400 responses to additional questions on courses, family background, information sources and post-study plans. Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas.

The biggest shift over three survey cycles is in who drives the decision. Self-motivated students rose from 29% in 2023-24 to 34% in 2024-25 and 49% in 2025-26. Family influence fell from 59% to 37% and then 36%. Younger students were more likely to rely on family guidance, while older applicants tended to decide independently. Self-motivation was highest in north and south India; family influence was strongest in the west and central region.

Academic choices were heavily concentrated. Seven in 10 were applying for postgraduate courses, and 75% identified business and management as their main field. Health and medicine was a distant second at 8%. Sciences accounted for 2% and engineering 1%.

Google searches led 39% of students to their institution, followed by agents (35%). But Google's lead widened on trust: 56% named it their most trusted source for education information, compared with 20% for college events and 9% for Instagram. AI tools were trusted most by 6% and YouTube by 5%.

World.title: India, China discuss LAC situation and border management during diplomatic talks: MEA
World.content:
India and China reviewed the overall situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and deliberated on key issues related to boundary delimitation, border management and trans-border cooperation.

It was underlined that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Friday (August 7, 2026), a day after the diplomatic talks between the two sides in New Delhi.

“The two sides engaged in frank discussions and reviewed the situation along the LAC,” it said.

The talks were held under the framework of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC).

“Both sides agreed to continue to use existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC,” the MEA said.

As a follow-up to the outcomes of the last edition of Special Representatives talks, the two sides held detailed exchanges on issues related to boundary delimitation, border management, mechanism-building and trans-border cooperation, it said in a statement.

The MEA said the Indian side reiterated the need for early convening of the next meeting of the expert-level mechanism on trans-border rivers and emphasised the importance of sharing technical details on upstream projects, it added.

The Indian delegation at the meeting was led by Sujit Ghosh, Joint Secretary (East Asia) in the MEA.

The Chinese delegation was led by Hou Yanqi, Director General of the Boundary and Oceanic Affairs Department at China’s Foreign Ministry.

World.title: Stable India-China ties will help build ‘multi-polar Asia’ and ‘multi-polar world’: Jaishankar
World.content:
Stable India-China relations will help foster a “multi-polar Asia” and a “multi-polar world”, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said during a meeting with his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in Manila. The meeting took place before the Foreign Ministers of the Quad countries, Australia, India, Japan, and the U.S., met on the sidelines of the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in the Philippine capital and reiterated their support for stability in the Indo-Pacific region. In a separate meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, held days after four Indian seafarers were killed in a Russian projectile strike in the Black Sea, Mr. Jaishankar expressed “strong concern” regarding the safety of Indian seafarers.

“We believe that a stable and cooperative relationship can best be developed on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity. Such a relationship can make a valuable contribution to a multi-polar Asia and a multi-polar world,” Mr. Jaishankar said in his remarks, highlighting that “peace and tranquillity in the border areas is obviously the pre-requisite for normal ties.”

The comments came against the backdrop of renewed India-China engagement, including the resumption of direct flights, updates to the visa regime, the restart of the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, and the resumption of border trade. In this context, Mr. Jaishankar said, “... the steps in normalisation taken over the last few months must be welcomed.” Mr. Jaishankar referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping’s meeting in Kazan in October 2024 and recalled that the two leaders had “agreed that differences should not become disputes”. “It is the duty of diplomacy to properly manage them,” he said. He also raised the importance of “predictability of supply chains” and “fair market access”, which need to be addressed.

The India-China ministerial discussion was followed by the meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Quad countries, Australia, India, Japan, and the U.S. on the sidelines of the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in the Philippine capital, which reiterated their support for stability in the Indo-Pacific region

The Ministry of External Affairs issued a joint press release on cooperation between the Quad members and the ASEAN countries, stating, “As ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partners we, the Secretary of State of the United States and the Foreign Ministers of Australia, India and Japan met today in Manila to reaffirm our commitment to strengthening a free and open Indo-Pacific and our unwavering support for ASEAN unity and centrality.” The Ministers discussed the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP), transnational security, economic opportunities, critical and emerging technologies, and HADR (Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief).

The expression of support for the ASEAN member countries came three days after a maritime confrontation between the Philippine Navy and the China Coast Guard at the Ren’ai Reef in the South China Sea. Both sides have accused each other of aggression at the Ren’ai Reef. China has summoned Manila’s Ambassador to Beijing and lodged a protest against what it described as a “deliberate provocation”. Earlier, on July 6, China test-fired a long-range missile from a submarine in the South China Sea. The missile flew over the Philippines, drawing concern from regional countries, including Australia.

The Quad Foreign Ministers also reiterated their support for stability in the Indo-Pacific maritime domain.

Mr. Jaishankar held an “in-depth review” of India-Russia bilateral relations with Mr. Lavrov and expressed “strong concern regarding the safety of Indian seafarers in the region”.

“Discussed various aspects of our partnership, including trade and investment, energy and connectivity, science and technology and mobility,” said Mr. Jaishankar about his meeting with Mr. Lavrov, which came days after four Indian seafarers were killed in a Russian projectile strike on a merchant vessel near Odesa. The two Ministers, accompanied by other diplomats, also exchanged views on the Ukraine crisis and the situation in the Gulf.

After meeting U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Mr. Jaishankar said the two sides discussed “trade and tariffs, energy, defence and security, critical minerals and artificial intelligence”.

Mr. Jaishankar also met counterparts from the ASEAN region, including Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa P. Lazaro. Following the meeting, both Mr. Jaishankar and Ms. Lazaro referred to defence and maritime security as key areas of bilateral cooperation. India has delivered the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile to the Philippines.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session: ‘No direction from the Chair’ for Amit Shah’s presence, says Rijiju as Opposition protests Home Minister’s absence
World.content:
Rajya Sabha proceedings were adjourned for about half an hour on Friday (August 7, 2026) morning as Opposition members continued to disrupt the House, demanding the presence of Home Minister Amit Shah to respond on police action on students who protested against the alleged NEET paper leak.

Opposition MPs led by the Congress raised slogans seeking the presence of the Home Minister in the House, which were countered by the Treasury benches. Amid the ruckus, Chairman C. P. Radhakrishnan adjourned the proceedings till 12 p.m.

Soon after the listed papers were laid on the table of the House, leader of the Opposition and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge raised the issue of the continued absence of the Home Minister from the House during the monsoon session, which started on July 20.

He said the government was not even respecting the Chairman's comments and insulting the House.

On Thursday (August 6, 2026), Mr. Radhakrishnan told Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju to "echo the sentiments of the Opposition" to Mr. Shah and "consider the request" for his presence in the House.

Opposition parties have been demanding a statement in the House from Shah on the July 20 police action on protesters marching towards Parliament.

Mr. Rijiju, however, said there was no direction from the Chair and that the Leader of the Opposition was misleading the House.

Mr. Rijiju told the protesting Opposition members in the Lok Sabha that Home Minister Amit Shah has been coming to Parliament every day, and it is not right to protest over his name every day. “Amit Shah ji is such a person whose name itself is enough to make terrorists shiver,” he said.

Ministers attend the Parliamentary proceedings according to the agenda of their Ministries, he said, adding the Opposition cannot decide which Minister will come to the House and when.

"You had given an observation," Mr. Rijiju told the Chairman. "No direction was given by the Chair."

He went on to state that the Congress and other Opposition parties raise slogans and then walk out of Parliament, and that he condemns this act.

Amid heavy sloganeering, the Lok Sabha passed a Bill pertaining to the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) industry. The House was adjourned until Monday (August 10, 2026).

(With PTI inputs.)

World.title: Raw Mango drops a handloom rap
World.content:
“Explaining handloom is like explaining religion, or the idea of India.” This was fashion and textile designer Sanjay Garg’s response when a Vogue reporter asked him to explain what handloom is to a novice.

While Indian textile secures a spot in the India-UK Free Trade Agreement, the future of handloom depends on more than just tariffs. It requires design, storytelling and global demand.

Homegrown designers like Garg have been putting local weaves on the global map. Through his label Raw Mango, Garg has helped position handloom within India’s luxury fashion.

To mark National Handloom Day on August 7, Raw Mango has collaborated with Bengaluru rapper and tennis player Adil Kalyanpur (A-KAL) on “Handloom Y’All”, a rap track celebrating India’s living textile traditions.

Edited excerpts from an interview with Garg and A-KAL:

How did this collaboration come about and who is this song really for — the fashion community, music fans, or people who’ve never thought about handlooms?

Sanjay Garg: This collaboration came about after we saw Adil’s rap around Women’s Day, which really spoke to us. We have always believed in collaborating with emerging artists and musicians, and felt that he would be the right fit for this.

For us, tradition is not something that passes with time. It is ongoing and constantly evolving. Nostalgia can be a part of tradition, but tradition itself is not fixed, it is an ongoing dialogue between the past, present and future. We see tradition as the future.

We have always believed in widening the circle of handloom. The people who already consume handloom are aware of its value; the larger question is how we bring more people into that circle. This song is really an attempt to do that, to introduce handloom to people who may not have thought about it before, in a language that feels contemporary and accessible.

Mahatma Gandhi made Khadi a powerful symbol of colonial resistance in India’s freedom struggle. What do handlooms symbolise for India in 2026; can fashion today still be a form of political or cultural expression?

Garg: For us, handloom can certainly be fashion, but it is also much bigger than that. It is one of India’s greatest strengths and an important part of our cultural identity. When we talk about Indian heritage, we often speak about our spices, colours, food and traditions, but textiles and handloom are equally fundamental to that story.

India has one of the largest handloom-weaving communities in the world and an extraordinary diversity of handwoven textiles. That makes handloom a very strong expression of who we are as a country. For us, this song is both a tribute to that heritage and an attempt to make people look at handloom as something living and relevant today, rather than something belonging only to the past.

Ahead of India’s 80th Independence Day, how does your song reinterpret the Khadi (and handloom) legacy for a generation that may know little about it history?

Garg: We wanted to keep the song simple and accessible rather than make it technically or academically heavy. There are some very basic but important facts about handloom that we wanted to put out there. My brief to Adil was to imagine that he was explaining handloom to a child who had never heard of it before. How would you introduce the idea to them in the simplest possible way? That became the starting point for the song.

Adil, how do you make a song about weaving and craft feel authentic rather than educational?

Adil Kalyanpur: The biggest challenge was that handlooms are a deeply traditional subject, and in today’s world they are not always seen as something “cool” or contemporary.

I like to rap for an impact so when I learnt that handlooms support millions of livelihoods across India and are such an important part of our cultural identity, I felt this was a story worth telling. That’s when the creative process really took over.

While rap is often associated with being rebellious or crude, I’ve always seen it as a great medium to communicate ideas, inspire conversations and create positive change.

Which handloom weave or textile tradition has the most ‘hip-hop energy’, and why?

Kalyanpur: Although I may be biased, my favourite handloom is Maheshwari, perhaps because that’s also my mother’s last name. And just like the weave she is very hip (and also high energy!)

World.title: Thailand school shooting, Seven killed, 15 wounded, police say
World.content:
‌Seven people ​were ⁠killed in a school ‌shooting ‌in ‌Thailand ⁠on ⁠Friday (August 7, 2026), including the ​gunman, ‌and 15 people were ‌wounded, Thai ​national police ⁠spokesperson Trairong Phiwphan ‌said.

Lt. Col. Dechrapee Kongdee Nonthaburi Provincial ‌Police Commander confirmed the casualties ‌to ⁠Reuters and said the suspected ⁠gunman had committed suicide. Among those injured were one teacher and three students, he ​said.

Thailand school shooting updates on August 7, 2026

The incident took ‌place in the Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi province. Police identified the perpetrator as a student.

In photos ‌circulated by emergency workers, students ​streamed out of the Debsirin Nonthaburi School, on the northwestern outskirts ⁠of Bangkok, as ambulances operated. In one photo, one person is seen ‌lying down on a stretcher outside an ambulance, while another is attended to by a medic.
